Secondary suites — Surrey (the core rule: Secondary suites in Surrey: a suite is an accessory unit inside a house, semi-detached home or duplex. It can be no more than 40% of the main home's floor area and can't be a separate strata lot. Only one suite is allowed per home, and none in a coach house or garden suite. One suite may be allowed in homes in small-scale multi-unit housing zones, including Comprehensive Development zones. Each application is checked for legal restrictions such as Land Use Contracts and building schemes. To be legal, a suite must meet the zoning, have building permits, meet the BC Building Code, and pay the secondary suite utility and service fees.

Manufactured-home parks run on tenancy l: Manufactured-home parks are governed by tenancy law, not strata law: the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act and its regulation apply, and the strata age-bylaw rules don't. A seller must give the buyer the written tenancy agreement and park rules, and selling means assigning the pad tenancy, which needs the park owner's consent.
For contrast — the strata rule that appl: By contrast, strata rules apply at Sea Ridge Bays. Exemptions cover existing residents, live-in caregivers and, since May 1, 2023, a younger spouse or partner, children under 19 in the resident's care, and adult children the resident cared for before they turned 19. Strata rental restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022.

Tenure decides: a park home carries pad: Ownership type decides the monthly cost: a park home pays pad rent, while Sea Ridge Bays pays a strata fee instead (listings say $210 a month including water). Confirm the current amount for a specific home in the tenancy agreement or the Form B.
Under s.42 of the Act, as the Province s: If a park is redeveloped, section 42 of the Act sets the steps: the landlord must first have all permits and approvals, then give 12 months' notice and pay $20,000 compensation on or before the effective date. Tenants can leave early with 10 days' written notice, can dispute the notice within 15 days, and in some cases can claim more, up to the home's assessed value minus the $20,000. If the landlord doesn't go ahead within a reasonable time, they owe a further payment of $5,000 or 12 months' rent, whichever is greater.

The Real Estate Development Marketing Ac: Under the Real Estate Development Marketing Act, you can cancel a presale purchase within 7 days of signing the agreement or receiving the disclosure statement, whichever is later, and your deposit must be held in trust. The disclosure statement, not the listing or the presentation centre, sets the completion date, the deposits and exactly what you're buying, so have a lawyer read it within those 7 days.

Buildings in White Rock, such as Foster Martin, fall under White Rock's own Zoning Bylaw No. 2506 (2024) and Official Community Plan No. 2220 (2017). In Surrey, small-scale multi-unit housing rules (July 8, 2024) allow up to 3 units on lots under 280 m², 4 on lots over 280 m², and up to 6 on eligible lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, and a secondary suite can be no more than 40% of the main home's floor area.

PTT / new-home exemption: general tiers: Property transfer tax: 1% on the first $200,000, 2% up to $2 million and 3% above that, plus another 2% on the residential part over $3 million. Examples: $500,000 → $8,000; $700,000 → $12,000; $800,000 → $14,000 ($6,000 for a first-time buyer who fully qualifies); $900,000 → $16,000; $1 million → $18,000; $1.2 million → $22,000; $1.5 million → $28,000; $1.8 million → $34,000; $2 million → $38,000; $3.5 million → $93,000. The newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000 and partial up to $1,150,000. It applies to new homes, not bare land.
Zoning on the Surrey side is set by Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, and the City plan is the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (Bylaw 21900, adopted June 15, 2026). Streamside setbacks are in Part 7A of the Zoning Bylaw and depend on the class of the stream. Servicing is under Bylaw 8830 (1986).

The one age-restricted strata ownership: The Waterfront is the only age-restricted strata building in Fort Langley: freehold strata (plan BCS3620), 4 storeys, 78 units, built in 2009 and zoned CD-55. Village plan: the Fort Langley Community: Village plan: Fort Langley is governed by the Fort Langley Community Plan (Bylaw No. 2527, 1987), updated by the 2025 OCP update (Bylaw 6200, adopted December 1, 2025). It says the single-family area will continue to develop at the minimum lot size of 930 m² where vacant land can be subdivided, and that densities shouldn't increase. That's part of why the village has just one purpose-built 55+ building.
Village fee-simple lots (the default for: Around the edges of the acreages, the village itself is mostly freehold houses on their own lots, under the Fort Langley Community Plan and Zoning Bylaw No. 2500. Lots in the village core are also in the Heritage Conservation Area. Village residential zoning includes R-1E.

Flood diligence: Ask the Township for th: Flooding: ask the Township for the property's flood information before you buy. A small low-rise condo building at the e: A small 3-storey condo building on the east side of the village, built by Lanstone Homes in 2018 or 2019 (a current listing says 2018; building records say 2019).
Listing records for homes in this stock: These are row homes on their own fee-simple lots at Bedford Landing, built in 2007: no strata corporation, no strata fee and no Form B. Bedford Landing is a mixed community of houses, row homes, townhomes, live/work townhomes and condos on the old McDonald Cedar Mill lands, so check the ownership type address by address; strata buildings and fee-simple row homes share the same community name.
Two tenures, two diligence tracks — this: Fort Langley has both strata and fee-simple attached homes, and the checks are different. For the strata complexes (Leah, Flatiron): the Form B, bylaws, depreciation report and contingency reserve. For the fee-simple Bedford Landing row homes: no strata, Form B or strata fees; instead, the Township's zoning, the Community Plan, heritage and design rules, and any covenants or building scheme on title apply. Check which one a Billy Brown Road address is before writing conditions into an offer; the community name won't tell you.
Coach houses are fee-simple, not strata:: Coach houses aren't strata. Under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, a coach house is a second home on the same fee-simple lot as the main house, on the same title, and it can't be sold separately. A Fort Langley coach house shouldn't be priced or marketed like a strata unit.
ALR edges — stratification is barred and: Farm land on the edges of the village is partly in the Agricultural Land Reserve. Homes on ALR land can't be stratified, so a "townhouse strata" on ALR land isn't a legal form. The ALC allows one additional home without an application if it meets the size rules (up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less, up to 186 m² on larger ones), subject to Township bylaws. Farm tax status has three income tiers: $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha, and $10,000 under 0.8 ha.
Village fee-simple lots (the default for: The village is mostly freehold houses on their own lots, under the Fort Langley Community Plan and Zoning Bylaw No. 2500. Lots in the village core are also in the Heritage Conservation Area. Village residential zoning includes R-1E.
Bedford Landing — the fee-simple lot fab: Bedford Landing, on Billy Brown Road along the Bedford Channel, is a mixed community on the old McDonald Cedar Mill lands (the mill opened in 1921 on an 88-acre riverfront property). Fee-simple row homes on their own lots, built in 2007, sit alongside strata buildings: The Village (EPS998), Waterfront (BCS3620) and the Flatiron live/work strata. The community name doesn't tell you whether a property is a fee-simple lot or a strata unit, so check each address.
Serviced versus unserviced — it splits b: Services differ: the village and Bedford Landing are on city water and sewer, while the acreages on the edges use wells and septic. Well reports are due within 90 days of building, changing or decommissioning a well, and wells can be looked up in the provincial GWELLS database. Septic systems follow Fraser Health's rules through an authorized person, with a filing before construction and a certification letter after.
Floodplain ground: Fort Langley is low-l: Fort Langley is low-lying. The Township says the Salmon River Pump Station protects the community from flooding, and its flood gates close when the Fraser River rises.

BC Assessment farm class — full three-ti: Farm tax status from BC Assessment: you need farm income of at least $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha on larger properties, or $10,000 on under 0.8 ha, with the application to the assessor by October 31. The core distinction — park rules are no: The key difference: park rules aren't strata bylaws, and there's no Form B for a pad rental. The Form B is a strata document that a strata corporation provides within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. A pad-rental park has no strata corporation. Instead, a park buyer checks the written site tenancy agreement, the park rules and the Manufactured Home Registry record.
Depreciation reports and CRF (strata onl: Depreciation reports and contingency reserves apply to stratas only. Since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must get a depreciation report every five years, and owners can't vote to skip it; since November 1, 2023, they must put at least 10% of the operating budget into the contingency reserve. Neither applies to a manufactured-home park, so there's no reserve fund behind a park home. That's why the park's own rules and plans for upkeep matter.

Township zoning and plans: Murrayville s: Zoning and plans: Murrayville is under Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500. Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 250: Small-scale housing in the Township (Bylaw No. 6020, adopted November 18, 2024): eligible lots can have 3 units if they're 280 m² or smaller, or 4 if they're between 280 m² and 4,050 m². To be eligible, a lot must be inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on city water and sewer, not heritage-designated and not in a transit-oriented area; larger lots don't qualify, and there's no 6-unit option. A secondary suite can be up to 120 m².
13-month trend, Langley community median: Langley medians over the 13 months from September 2025 to September 2026: detached homes ranged from $1,315,000 (August 2026) to $1,455,000 (January 2026), and condos and townhomes from $611,000 (September 2026, the low) to $725,000 (June 2026) (SnapStats).
REDMA rescission and deposits — central: Your rights on a presale: under the Real Estate Development Marketing Act, you can cancel by written notice to the developer within seven days of signing the agreement or receiving the disclosure statement, whichever is later. The developer must give you the filed disclosure statement, and any amendments, before you sign, and your deposit must be held in trust.
Municipal zoning and plans — two Langley: Presales in Langley are in either the Township or the City, and the rules differ. In the Township, the Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 1842) was most recently updated by Bylaw No. 6200 on December 1, 2025, and zoning is under Bylaw No. 2500, including small-scale housing (Bylaw No. 6020: 3 units on eligible lots of 280 m² or less and 4 on lots from 280 m² to 4,050 m², with no 6-unit option; suites up to 120 m²). The Willoughby Community Plan (Bylaw 1836) is now part of Bylaw 6200. Updates to it had only first and second reading on May 25, 2026, so they aren't law yet.

Township rules (projects on Township gro: Township rules (for projects in the Township): zoning is under Bylaw No. 2500. Langley City frame (projects on City gro: Projects in the City of Langley follow the City's own rules: Zoning Bylaw No. 3300, small-scale housing Bylaw 3284, and a suite cap of 100 m² or 40% of the floor area, whichever is smaller.
Strata block (a completed bare-land stra: Strata rules (once a strata exists): the Form B must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page; since July 1, 2024, stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years; since November 1, 2023, at least 10% of the budget must go into the contingency reserve; rental restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022; and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable. The project's own ground decides: Townsh: Where the project is decides the rules. On MLS®: \"Otter District\" is one of el: On MLS®, Otter District is one of eleven Langley sub-areas. The board's "Langley" area combines the Township and the City of Langley, and Otter District is entirely in the Township.
Where the condo stock concentrates: ther: There are no condos here. The board counted no condo or townhome listings in September 2026, mainly because much of the district is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, where homes can't be stratified.
The ALR frame — the governing fact for m: Much of this district is in the Agricultural Land Reserve. ALR land can generally have only one home unless it qualifies for an additional one, and the Township can restrict homes further through zoning. The main house can be up to 500 m². A suite is only allowed if it's entirely inside the main house (a separate building isn't a suite) and local bylaws allow it. One additional detached home is allowed without an application, up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on larger ones, subject to local bylaws. ALR homes can't be stratified. Check a specific property's ALR status on the Agricultural Land Commission's map.
ALR housing frame: On ALR land the princ: ALR homes: on Agricultural Land Reserve land, the main house can be up to 500 m² (with no more than 1,000 m² of fill to build it), a suite is only allowed entirely inside the main house, and one additional detached home is allowed without an application, up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on larger ones, subject to local bylaws. Check a specific property's ALR status on the Agricultural Land Commission's map; the district name doesn't tell you. A couple of current listings mention ALR status for their own parcels.
The district's park looks like seniors p: Langley Grove Estates looks like a seniors' park, with a clubhouse and amenities, but its listings say there are no age restrictions. I don't know of any 55+ homes of any kind in Otter District.
A \"coach house\" here has a narrow lega: "Coach house" has a narrow meaning here: under Township Bylaw No. 2500, a coach house is only on the second storey of a detached garage. A ground-floor detached suite on an Otter acreage is a different kind of unit with different rules, whatever the listing calls it.
Not on ALR land within the ALC frame: AL: Not on ALR land. Creating a strata counts as subdividing, and agricultural land can't be subdivided without the Agricultural Land Commission's permission, so homes on ALR land can't be stratified.
The documented stock is freehold acreage: The homes here are freehold acreages and the park homes at Langley Grove Estates. An acreage listed with two homes on it needs checking under the ALR rules for a second home; it isn't a duplex.
Parks and facilities: the Salmon River N: Parks and facilities: the Salmon River Natural Area is a Township park. There's no recreation centre or library in the district itself; the nearest are in Fort Langley and Walnut Grove. There are few or no stores here; the nearest grocer is Lee's Market, 23320 Mavis Avenue, Fort Langley.
Three routes, kept separate: (1) on ALR: There are three different routes to a second home: on ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission's additional-home rule above; under the Township's small-scale housing rules, a suite or accessory unit, depending on zoning, with suites capped at 120 m²; or a coach house on the second storey of a detached garage, which is part of the fee-simple lot, never strata.
SD35, address-based. The settled sample: Schools are in SD35, and catchments are set by address. For example, 4452 256 Street is in the catchment for North Otter Elementary and D.W. Poppy Secondary. Coghlan Fundamental Elementary, at that same address, is a district choice school on the upland east side. I don't know of any school inside the valley itself. Check the exact address with the school district before relying on a school.
Only at the edge: route 562 runs on Glov: Only at the edge. Route 562 runs on Glover Road at the Fort Langley end (Langley Centre to Walnut Grove and Carvolth Exchange), but no bus runs on the valley roads, and there's no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in the district. You'll need a car.
Serviced vs unserviced — well/septic gro: Water and sewer: rural properties here may use wells and septic. Look up a property's well in GWELLS, the provincial database of registered wells and aquifers; well reports are due within 90 days of building, changing or decommissioning a well. Unless the Township confirms a property is on city services, plan on checking the well and septic.
Market context: Langley is a SnapStats-c: Market figures: in September 2026, 22 detached homes were listed in Salmon River and 5 sold (23%, one of the stronger rates in rural Langley, though from few listings), and 4 condos and townhomes were listed with none sold. The board doesn't publish medians for Salmon River; the Langley-wide medians were $1,345,000 for detached homes and $611,000 for condos and townhomes. It also doesn't publish land prices.
R-CL s.403 (where it applies): 220 m² mi: Compact R-CL lots, where that zone applies, are 220 m² to 464.5 m² under Zoning Bylaw 2500. That zone and the Willoughby plan are for Willoughby, not Salmon River.
ALR and flood — the governing facts for: ALR and flooding: some farm land in the valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, so check a specific property on the Agricultural Land Commission's map. On ALR land, the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite must be entirely inside it, and one additional home is allowed without an application, up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on larger ones, subject to Township bylaws. The valley is on the Fraser River floodplain. The Township says the Salmon River Pump Station was built to help prevent flooding of the farmland during the spring freshet, and its flood gates close when the Fraser River rises. Council has approved design and tendering for upgrades to the station.
Willoughby Community Plan, origin and cu: The Willoughby Community Plan started as Bylaw 1836 (1979) and is now part of Bylaw 6200 (adopted December 1, 2025). The Township's 2026 update proposes a new Willoughby Community Plan (Bylaw No. 6201), a Willoughby Transit Corridor Plan (Bylaw No. 6202, combining the Carvolth, Latimer, Jericho, Routley and Southwest Gordon Estate plans) and a Gordon Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 6203, combining the Central and Northeast Gordon Estate plans), plus a new development permit area for transit-oriented development. Check the current status of these with the Township.
Zoning and SSMUH (Township): zoning is u: Zoning in the Township is under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500. Small-scale housing (Bylaw No. 6020, adopted November 18, 2024) allows 3 units on eligible lots of 280 m² or less and 4 on lots from 280 m² to 4,050 m², with no 6-unit option, and since April 27, 2026 a development permit area sets design guidelines for it. To be eligible, a lot must be inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on city water and sewer, not heritage-designated, not in a transit-oriented area and no larger than 4,050 m². Suites are capped at 120 m². The Township's one transit-oriented area is on 196 Street in Willowbrook, around the proposed Surrey–Langley SkyTrain station; designated by the Province on May 2, 2025, it allows minimum densities of 8 to 20 storeys within 800 m, depending on distance from the station.
The plan stack a Township parcel can sit: A Township property can be covered by several layers: the Official Community Plan (updated by Bylaw No. 6200 on December 1, 2025), a community plan, a neighbourhood plan where there is one, Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (including small-scale housing Bylaw No. 6020), and development permit areas such as the one for small-scale housing adopted April 27, 2026. A plan designation is policy; it doesn't mean serviced lots or land for sale.

Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere: There are no condos on Barnston Island. Homes here are a small number of farmhouses and rural houses on large farm properties. Metro Vancouver puts the island's population at about 150, and it has been farmed since the mid-1800s.
Planning authority: Metro Vancouver, not: Barnston Island isn't part of a city. Metro Vancouver plans and zones it as part of Electoral Area A. Its Official Community Plan (2018) aims to keep the island a thriving farming community, and doesn't apply to First Nations reserve land. There are no large developments.
Farm classification (BC Assessment) — st: Farm tax status from BC Assessment depends on the size of the operation: $2,500 of farm income for 0.8–4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha for larger operations, and $10,000 for under 0.8 ha, with applications due by October 31.
What land actually is here: a small stoc: Homes here are a small number of farmhouses and rural houses on large farm properties, mostly older. Metro Vancouver's 2019 farm study puts the population at about 150, and the island has been farmed since the mid-1800s. The plan keeps lots large, so small-lot subdivision isn't expected.
Legal geography, restated because everyt: Most of the island is unincorporated Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A. The southeast part is Barnston Island Indian Reserve No. 3 (Katzie First Nation), which is federal reserve land, not homes for sale on the open market. Nearby: Port Kells in Surrey at the ferry landing, and Pitt Meadows across the main channel (no direct connection).

"Bear Creek Green Timbers" isn't one of the City's seven communities (City Centre, Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey and Whalley); it's the real estate board's name.
Streamside / riparian — the creek dilige: Streams: Surrey sets streamside setbacks in Part 7A of Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, by type of stream, along with a sensitive ecosystems development permit. Bear Creek Green Timbers is one Fraser V: Bear Creek Green Timbers is a single real estate board area with a two-part name, not two separate neighbourhoods: Bear Creek Park on the west side and Green Timbers Urban Forest on the east.
One board sub-area with a compound name: Bear Creek Green Timbers is one area in the real estate board's Surrey figures, joining Bear Creek Park (which the City places in Whalley) and Green Timbers Urban Forest. It isn't one of the City's seven community names.
Different permissions: SSMUH allows 3–4: Building more units and creating lots are different things. Bear Creek Green Timbers is one area with a two-part name. It joins Bear Creek Park, which the City places in Whalley beside the Surrey Arts Centre, with Green Timbers Urban Forest to the east. People mention the two parks separately, but listings and market figures use the combined name.
Bear Creek Green Timbers is one board su: Bear Creek Green Timbers is one of 15 areas the real estate board uses for Surrey, not two separate areas. Transit: the Surrey Langley SkyTrain pro: Transit: the Surrey Langley SkyTrain's Green Timbers Station will be at 140 Street and Fraser Highway, at the west edge of Green Timbers Urban Forest, near the Jim Pattison Outpatient Care and Surgery Centre, the BC RCMP headquarters and Surrey Memorial Hospital. Form B diligence (all 3 strata complexes: For all three strata complexes, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. For Carlingwood (around 2000) and the Trails townhouses (1994–1995), the depreciation report matters most; the Kings Landing townhomes (2016–2020) are much newer.

In one cluster: Kings Landing (13628 81A: The condos are in one cluster on 81A Avenue, south of Bear Creek Park: Kings Landing (13628 81A Avenue, built 2020) and Kings Landing II (13623 81A Avenue, 112 condos in a 6-storey wood-frame building, built 2021), both by Dawson + Sawyer. Pets: pet limits remain lawful strata by: Pets: strata pet limits are still allowed. BC strata rules (wherever a bare-land st: If you're buying a bare-land strata lot (I don't know of any in Clayton), BC strata rules apply: check the Form B, depreciation report and contingency reserve before you buy. The farm zones are confirmed on a City o: Surrey's farm zones are A-1 General Agriculture and A-2 Intensive Agriculture, under Zoning Bylaw No. 12000.
Transit: No rapid-transit station is in: Transit: there's no SkyTrain station in Cloverdale. Lot character: there is no Cloverdale-wi: Lot sizes: there's no single lot-size rule for Cloverdale. ALR vs non-ALR split: The Cloverdale com: Cloverdale includes Agricultural Land Reserve farmland on its lowland side. Clayton's 9: Sun @ 72; Clayton Walk; The: The nine Clayton complexes: Sun @ 72, Clayton Walk, The Grove (not the same as The Grove condos in Walnut Grove), Creekside, Ixia, The Belmont, Balmoral, The Edge and Montana.

Location as the City states it: Cloverda: The City describes Cloverdale as Surrey's third-largest community: its western border is 160 Street, its southern border is 48 Avenue, Langley is to the east, and Guildford and Fleetwood are to the north, along 84 Avenue and 76 Avenue.
Character as the City states it: the his: The City describes Cloverdale as the historic centre of Surrey: settled in the mid to late 1800s, it grew from a rural farming community named after Clover Valley into a railway and commercial hub, and has hosted the Cloverdale Rodeo at the fairgrounds since 1945.
Serviced vs unserviced ground: the urban: The town core is on city water and sewer. On the rural farm edge, services vary by property, so check each one.

Zoning, SSMUH and suites (Surrey): The C: Zoning and suites in Surrey: up to 3 units on lots under 280 m², 4 on lots over 280 m², and up to 6 on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. One secondary suite is allowed per house, up to 40% of the main home's floor area; properties without city water and sewer are among the exceptions. The new rules don't legalize a suite or coach house built without permits, so check the permits for any suite in an East Newton listing.
A mixed community: apartment-style condo: A gated 55+ community on 23 acres with condos at 13870 70 Avenue and ground-level townhomes at 13888 70 Avenue, all strata (plan LMS1416). Age bylaws — 55+ is the only legal form:: Age bylaws: the only legal one is 55 and older. Secondary suites — the 40% cap: Surrey's: Suites: Surrey caps a secondary suite at 40% of the main home's floor area. An existing East Newton townhouse doesn't gain a legal lock-off suite from that change.
The 55+ townhouse supply here is two com: There are only two 55+ townhouse options here: Charleston Green (1988) and the townhouses at Chelsea Gardens. Sullivan Mews also shows up in 55+ searches, but it's a cash-only membership, not a townhouse you buy.
Coverage is building-by-building and is: Insurance coverage varies by building and is shown on the Form B, along with the monthly fee and contingency reserve balance. The strata must provide it within 7 days. Don't rely on the fee in the listing alone.

Not land stock — townhouse ground: Nora: Nora (12830 62 Avenue, 42 townhouses, 2022), Steller Panorama (5858 132 Street, 39 townhouses, 2022) and The Uplands (15152 62A Avenue, 124 townhouses, 2005) are strata townhouse complexes on Panorama Ridge, not land for sale.

Geography trap, stated here: Barnston Is: Barnston Island isn't in Surrey: it's Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A plus Katzie First Nation reserve land. The real estate board files it under Port Kells only because the ferry lands at the foot of 104 Avenue in Port Kells.
Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere: There are no condos in Port Kells. Homes are mostly freehold detached houses on suburban and larger rural lots, plus cluster housing shown in the South Port Kells Land Use Plan. North of Highway 1 it's industrial, not housing.
City plan and zoning: Surrey 2050 Offici: Plans and zoning: Surrey's current Official Community Plan is Surrey 2050 (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026). Schools (SD36): Port Kells Elementary (K: Schools (SD36): Port Kells Elementary (K–7), 19076 88 Avenue, serves the area. Its building opened in 1907 and is on the Canadian Register of Historic Places. Catchments are set by address, so check a specific home with the school district.
Form B diligence (any strata purchase —: I don't know of any strata homes in Port Kells today, but for any strata purchase, including in nearby Guildford or Fleetwood, read the Form B. It shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. ALR frame: ALR lands run through the Sou: Agricultural Land Reserve land runs through South Port Kells. ALR homes can't be stratified. On ALR land, the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is only allowed inside it, and an additional home can be up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² on larger ones. Check whether a south-side property is in the ALR before counting on a second home.
Character, as the City states it: North: North Port Kells is mostly light industrial: the City profiles it as one of Surrey's major industrial areas, with about 610 businesses across 781 acres, mainly manufacturing, construction and wholesale. It's warehouses, work yards and industrial buildings, not housing.
Character, as the plan states it: the re: Homes are concentrated in South Port Kells: detached houses on suburban and larger rural lots, plus areas planned for cluster housing in the South Port Kells Land Use Plan. "Cluster housing" is a plan designation, not an existing complex or lots for sale.
SSMUH / subdivision potential (Surrey, a: Small-scale housing in Surrey (since July 8, 2024): up to 3 units on lots under 280 m², 4 on lots over 280 m², and up to 6 on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, for eligible lots under 4,050 m² inside the Urban Containment Boundary. These rules don't override ALR status on farmland, and they don't legalize a suite or coach house built without permits.
A bare-land strata lot is strata tenure: A bare-land strata lot is strata ownership: BC strata rules apply, so check the Form B, depreciation report and contingency reserve, and note that rental bans are void and only 55+ age bylaws are valid. On ALR land, homes can't be stratified at all.
Both things are true: it is a real FVREB: Port Kells is one of the real estate board's areas, and the City profiles it as a major industrial area. It isn't one of Surrey's six town centres.
Port Kells is one of the real estate board's areas, and the City profiles it as a major industrial area. It isn't one of Surrey's six town centres; for planning, it's grouped with the Guildford area.
A gated manufactured-home park; listings: A gated 55+ manufactured-home park, described in listings as "one of Surrey's most premier, sought after manufactured home parks", with a clubhouse. Listings give the address as both 8224 and 8254 134 Street, so confirm the address and pad number with the park office. City zoning: Surrey Zoning By-law, 1993,: Zoning: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 applies to every property here. Check a specific property's zone on the City's COSMOS map.
Plans: the Surrey 2050 Official Communit: Plans: Surrey's current Official Community Plan is Surrey 2050 (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026), which replaced the 2013 plan. Older neighbourhood plan designations across Newton have been folded into or replaced by it, so check the current OCP and Zoning Bylaw 12000 rather than old plan documents.
By Whitetail Homes, the companion buildi: Gabriel, by Whitetail Homes, is the companion building to Galilea on 94A and 95 Avenue: six storeys and 125 condos over two levels of underground parking, completed in 2026. Listings describe the homes as move-in ready and say cats are allowed.
Zoning and plan status: Surrey Zoning By: Zoning and plans: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 applies, under the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026). Queen Mary Park has no neighbourhood plan of its own, so there's no plan designation to quote for these buildings.
Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) a: Small-scale housing and suites: Surrey allows 3 units on lots under 280 m², 4 on lots over 280 m², and up to 6 on eligible lots of 281 m² or more within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. With RapidBus routes R1 and R6 on its edges, much of this area is close enough to qualify. One secondary suite is allowed per house, but the new rules don't legalize a suite built without permits, and several house listings here openly describe unauthorized suites.
The townhouse stock is old, and that is: Most of the townhouse complexes here are old: Bonnydoon Village (1974), Barkerville II (1988), Hadley Green (1989) and Lakewood Grove (1991), with Kennedy Trail (2008) the exception. That makes the depreciation report and contingency reserve balance more important here than in Surrey's newer townhouse areas.
ALR block — conditional, no ALR ground d: I don't know of any Agricultural Land Reserve land in this area. If a property were in the ALR: homes can't be stratified, subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, the main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, and one additional home can be up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on larger ones. Farm tax status has three income tiers: $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha, and $10,000 under 0.8 ha, with applications due by October 31.
The defining stock fact is the downzoned: Royal Heights' defining feature is its downzoning: all 127 lots in the Royal Heights Park neighbourhood are under one Comprehensive Development zone (Bylaw No. 16419), which caps house size and height. There's more detail in the Royal Heights houses for sale guide.
Coach houses and garden suites (Surrey,: Coach houses and garden suites in Surrey (not on ALR land): allowed in all residential zones that allow detached houses, duplexes and houseplexes. They can be 35–75 m², or up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots where the house or duplex is below the maximum floor area. Smaller R3–R6 lots need lane access, and one extra parking space is required.
City zoning and OCP: Surrey Zoning By-la: Zoning and plans: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 applies; check a property's zone on the City's COSMOS map. The current Official Community Plan is Surrey 2050 (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026).
Ownership itself is not age-restricted —: A 55+ bylaw limits who can live in a home, not who can own it: the Province says people under 55 can own a strata unit in a 55+ building but may not be able to live in it. That applies to the South Surrey and Cloverdale complexes, not to Serpentine's acreages, which have no age rules.
Board figures (with the conflict carried: Market figures, September 2026: Serpentine had no detached homes, condos or townhomes listed or sold. Nearby, Clayton had 34 detached listed and 10 sold (29%) and 96 attached listed and 20 sold (21%); Cloverdale had 167 detached listed and 22 sold (13%) and 98 attached listed and 17 sold (17%). The board doesn't publish medians for individual areas.
Depreciation reports and CRF (strata sto: Depreciation reports and contingency reserves apply to strata: since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots need a depreciation report every five years, and since November 1, 2023 at least 10% of the operating budget must go into the reserve. There are no strata homes in this area.
The Campbell Heights parcels' \"developm: Some Campbell Heights listings describe "development or industrial-side opportunity". That's the seller's marketing; there's no known land assembly, rezoning or development proposal behind it.
South Surrey's one settled school run is: School catchments are set by address. A School Locator check for 1785 148 Street gives H.T. Thrift Elementary and Semiahmoo Secondary, but that says nothing about a farm on 176 Street, so check the exact address.

These are Cloverdale-wide figures, not Serpentine's. Clayton was the fastest-moving area that month (29% of detached and 21% of attached listings sold).
City zoning: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 120: Zoning: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 applies. Chelsea Gardens, next door, is zoned RM45.
There is no known 55+ housing of any kin: I don't know of any 55+ housing in Sullivan Station. The complexes here are family townhouses and condos.
Sullivan Mews at 15020 66A Avenue is a g: Sullivan Mews, at 15020 66A Avenue, is a real 55+ community, but it's in the East Newton area, not Sullivan Station, and it isn't strata. You buy a membership, so instead of a strata lot and Form B, you review the membership documents.
Fee-simple detached lots — the land form: Most land here is fee-simple detached lots: no strata, Form B or strata fees. Before buying, check the title, the zone, how many units the lot allows, and any streamside area on the property. South Newton is mostly R-series residential zoning, with RA (acreage) at the rural edges toward Colebrook, under Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000.
Assemblies / development sites: The docu: Development sites: the old South Newton plan has been rescinded. Land use designations were updated by a Corporate Report endorsed December 2, 2024, so a site's potential depends on the Surrey 2050 OCP and Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, not the old plan.
Municipality and community: City of Surr: Sullivan Station is in the City of Surrey's Newton community. It's the real estate board's name for the area; the City has no separate Sullivan Station plan boundary. The City describes South Newton as a large neighbourhood in southeast Newton, with shopping nodes at Panorama Heights (152 Street and Highway 10) and Sullivan Heights (64 Avenue and 144 Street), and Sullivan Station is within it.
The plan most sellers still name no long: The plan many sellers still mention no longer exists. The South Newton plan was rescinded when Surrey 2050 came in, so a lot marketed "per the South Newton NCP" is quoting a dead plan. What applies now is Surrey 2050 (Bylaw No. 21900) and the designation updates of December 2, 2024. That's the most important land fact in this area.
Sullivan Station is a residential sub-ar: Sullivan Station is a residential area in the City of Surrey's Newton community. It's the real estate board's name for the area; the City has no separate Sullivan Station plan boundary.
Build years vary by unit in the listings: Build years vary by unit, from 2014 to 2016. A current listing says up to two cats or dogs are allowed, with restrictions; confirm on the Form B.

Many of the 1970s low-rises around the core are rental buildings, not strata.

How Surrey's plan system is organized: t: How Surrey's plans work: the City groups its approved plans by community (South Surrey, Newton, Cloverdale, Whalley, Guildford and Fleetwood, among others). Each was developed with community input and endorsed by Council, and sets out land uses, density, roads, amenities and servicing. A General Land Use Plan is the overall framework for an area; a Neighbourhood Concept Plan is the detailed plan under it; and a Local Area Plan does the same job outside that process.
OCP — current bylaw: Surrey 2050, Offici: Surrey's current Official Community Plan is Surrey 2050 (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026), and zoning is under Bylaw No. 12000. Surrey 2050 rescinded the East Newton North plan and replaced the land use designations in the East Newton South, East Newton Business Park and West Cloverdale plans. The OCP now guides land use there, while those plans still guide amenities and infrastructure.
Short-term rentals: permitted, owner-onl: Short-term rentals are allowed only in the owner's principal residence; tenants can't run one, and the owner needs a City business licence first. The licence is about $358 a year; check the City's licence page for the current amount.

GST / PTT / programs (resale frame): all: Taxes and programs: all five complexes are resales, so there's no GST. For new homes, such as the Harth presale, the new-home programs apply: the First-Time Home Buyers' GST rebate (all the GST up to $1 million, phasing out at $1.5 million, maximum $50,000, for agreements signed from March 20, 2025 to the end of 2030), the New Housing Rebate (36%, up to $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000), and the newly built home transfer tax exemption (full to $1,100,000, ending at $1,150,000). For any first home, the first-time buyer transfer tax exemption covers the first $500,000 (full to $835,000, partial to $860,000), and the Home Buyers' Plan ($60,000) and FHSA ($8,000 a year up to $40,000) can help with the down payment. CMHC insurance premiums run 0.6%–4.5%.

On urban ground: one secondary suite in: In the urban area: one secondary suite is allowed in any single detached house on a lot of at least 400 m² with 12 m of frontage, on a collector or local road and not on a cul-de-sac bulb. On ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission's limits apply instead: a main house of up to 500 m², a suite only inside it, and an additional home of 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on larger ones.

Urban lots: the detached stock across th: House lots across the urban west side are freehold, mostly in the RS residential zones (RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m², RS5 420 m²). A bare lot in Clearbrook, Peardonville or Townline is fee simple: no strata, Form B or strata fee, with zoning, the OCP and any covenants or building scheme on title setting the rules.
ALR rules, on the west/southwest edge: s: ALR rules on the west and southwest edge: subdividing in the Agricultural Land Reserve needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR homes can't be stratified, so no bare-land strata can be created from ALR land here. The main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is only allowed inside it, and an additional home can be up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² on larger ones. The City's A1 farm zone allows one additional farm home per lot of at least 0.4 ha, under the same ALR rules and size limits.
Bare-land strata rules (apply to every D: Every Downes Road Estates lot is bare-land strata, so strata rules apply. Read the Form B (strata fee, amounts owing, approved levies, contingency reserve balance, parking and storage, and an insurance summary), which the strata must provide within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Since July 1, 2024, stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, and since November 1, 2023 at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans have been void since November 24, 2022, and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, so the "45+" in some marketing isn't an enforceable bylaw; the registered bylaws are what count.
First-home programs — the land boundary,: First-home programs apply to homes, not land. The First-Time Home Buyers' GST rebate refunds all the GST on a new home up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out at $1.5 million, for agreements signed from March 20, 2025 to the end of 2030. A Downes Road Estates resale or a rural lot doesn't qualify. The older GST New Housing Rebate (36%, up to $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000) is also only for homes. The Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000 per buyer, and an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000.

Headline fact: Aberdeen has no known con: Aberdeen has no condos. The only strata homes in the area are one townhome complex at its western edge. If you need a condo, look in Abbotsford West or Central Abbotsford.
Why no condos — agricultural zoning and: Why there are no condos: rural Aberdeen is zoned for farming (A1, with a minimum lot size for subdividing of 8 ha, and A2, 16 ha), and the land is in or beside the Agricultural Land Reserve. Subdividing, non-farm uses and extra homes need City approval and, where the ALR rules require it, Agricultural Land Commission approval.
The one strata complex (Lantern Park tow: The one strata complex, Lantern Park, follows strata rules: you'll get the Form B package, and the BC Real Estate Association recommends checking it for the latest depreciation report, financial statements, contingency reserve balance and planned work.
Presales (REDMA), HBP/FHSA, CMHC — for r: If you buy elsewhere in Abbotsford: presales come with a 7-day right to cancel and deposits held in trust. The Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000 per buyer, and an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000. CMHC insurance premiums run 0.60%–4.00% depending on your down payment (4.50% at the top tier with a non-traditional down payment), plus 0.20% for amortizations over 25 years.
Aberdeen Elementary is the area's one sc: Aberdeen Elementary is the area's one school. The SD34 School Locator for its address (2975 Bradner Road) gives Aberdeen Elementary, Eugene Reimer Middle and Rick Hansen Secondary, the same path the district publishes, which is useful for acreage buyers.
23 homes in 3 storeys, built 2021, wood-: Lantern Park: 23 three-storey wood-frame townhomes by the Reimer Group, built in 2021. Freehold strata (plan EPS7130), managed by Associa, with visitor parking and single or double garages. The strata fee covers snow removal, management, gardening and garbage pickup, and the 2-5-10 new-home warranty runs to 2031.
Ministry-confirmed addresses for the cha: Eugene Reimer Middle School is at 3433 Firhill Drive, in Abbotsford West. Catchments are set by SD34 policy.
Form B diligence (Lantern Park): Strata: For Lantern Park, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. The BC Real Estate Association recommends checking the depreciation report, financial statements, reserve balance and planned work.
Why there is no more townhouse stock — a: Why there aren't more townhouses: rural Aberdeen is zoned for farming (A1, minimum 8 ha to subdivide; A2, 16 ha; check a lot's zone on the City's WebMap), and the land is in or beside the Agricultural Land Reserve. Subdividing, non-farm uses and extra homes need City approval and, where the ALR rules require it, Agricultural Land Commission approval. ALR homes can't be stratified. Floodplain status also varies by lot, so check each one.
Farm-class thresholds (full three-tier f: Farm tax status: you need farm income of $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha on larger properties, or $10,000 on under 0.8 ha, with applications due by October 31.
Fee-simple lots are the default — effect: Homes in Aberdeen are almost all freehold detached houses on rural and farm lots. Abbotsford's zoning bylaw applies, including the farm zones: A1 has a minimum lot size of 8 ha for subdividing, and A2 has 16 ha (check a lot's zone on the City's WebMap). At those sizes, there are no new lots or condo buildings coming.
Schools: Aberdeen Elementary, 2975 Bradn: Schools: Aberdeen Elementary, 2975 Bradner Road, is the public elementary school in the area. The SD34 School Locator for that address gives Aberdeen Elementary, Eugene Reimer Middle (3433 Firhill Drive, in Abbotsford West) and Rick Hansen Secondary (Grades 9–12), the same path Eugene Reimer Middle publishes for its feeder schools.
Only one chain is settled, single-addres: One example: 2975 Bradner Road is in the catchment for Aberdeen Elementary, Eugene Reimer Middle and Rick Hansen Secondary.
Municipal law here is District of Kent l: Agassiz is governed by the District of Kent. Zoning is under Kent Zoning Bylaw No. 1219 (2001), and the District's 2025 Official Community Plan designates the townsite core as Town Centre and directs growth there. Bylaw No. 1737 (adopted June 10, 2024) created the RS1 zone, which allows up to four homes on serviced residential lots in Agassiz without rezoning, subject to conditions. Secondary suites are allowed in single-family homes in all residential zones.
Fresh verification: a current listing (M: A current listing describes a townhome in a private, well-kept complex with mountain views, a double garage, a fenced yard and "low strata fees". No rental, pet or age restrictions are published.
Fresh verification by name found every n: Every named strata complex in the townsite is townhouses: Village Gate, The Langtry, Fraser Green, Gallagher Landing, Town Centre Gable, MountView and Huckleberry Lane. I don't know of any condo buildings.
None that I know of. No public source st: None that I know of. No Agassiz townhouse complex has a published 55+ bylaw, and Huckleberry Lane's listing says "no age restrictions". The town's 55+ options are a bare-land strata of detached ranchers (Maplewood Village) and rental or care housing, not townhouses.
The catchment question for Bradner was u: Bradner's school catchment used to be unclear: one district map named W.A. Fraser Middle for 5396 Bradner Road, while Eugene Reimer's school pages named Reimer. A School Locator check confirms Eugene Reimer Middle, so the path is Bradner Elementary, Eugene Reimer Middle and Rick Hansen Secondary.
No stratification in the ALR without ALC: Homes on ALR land can't be stratified without Agricultural Land Commission permission, because creating a strata counts as subdividing farmland. That's the main reason there are no townhouses in Bradner.
Bare-land strata: none — and structurall: Bare-land strata: there isn't any in Bradner, and it can't be created on ALR land. Where it exists elsewhere, strata rules, fees and a Form B apply to the lot.
Schools are address-based in SD34; the o: School catchments in SD34 are set by address. For 5396 Bradner Road, the middle school is Eugene Reimer Middle, not W.A. Fraser.
Farm class (BC Assessment) — the full th: Farm tax status from BC Assessment: you need farm income of $2,500 on an operation of 0.8–4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the farm value over 4 ha on larger operations, or $10,000 on under 0.8 ha, with applications due by October 31. Farm status makes a big difference to property tax on a working Bradner farm versus an idle one, so check the property's current class and income record before working out the taxes.
If a strata purchase is made elsewhere i: If you buy a strata home elsewhere in Abbotsford, BC strata rules apply: check the Form B, depreciation report and contingency reserve, and note that rental bans are void and only 55+ age bylaws are valid. None of this applies to a fee-simple property in Bradner: no strata, no Form B, no strata fees.
The middle-school correction is already: Some marketing still names the wrong middle school. A district boundary map named W.A. Fraser Middle for 5396 Bradner Road, but the School Locator and Eugene Reimer Middle's own pages both give Bradner Elementary, Eugene Reimer Middle and Rick Hansen Secondary.
Why duplexes are limited here: Bradner l: Why duplexes are limited: Bradner is zoned A1 and A2 for farming under Abbotsford's zoning bylaw, and part of it is in the Agricultural Land Reserve. On ALR land, homes can't be stratified without Agricultural Land Commission permission, because creating a strata counts as subdividing farmland.
A gated bare-land strata resort communit: The Cottages at Bridal Falls is a gated bare-land strata resort. Listings describe freehold strata lots zoned CD1, serviced with gas, hydro, water and sewer, with concrete pads, for full-time or lock-and-go use, plus a clubhouse, outdoor pool, hot tub, fitness centre and tennis courts. The cottages are single-storey homes on their own strata lots, not condos. A 2020 advertisement described the resort as 100 lots on almost 8 acres.
Transit: BC Transit route 71 (Agassiz–Ha: Transit: BC Transit route 71 (Agassiz–Harrison) runs between downtown Chilliwack and Harrison Hot Springs through Rosedale, and on-request trips can stop at Bridal Falls. There's no regular stop on every trip.
The Cottages at Bridal Falls / Bridal Fa: The Cottages at Bridal Falls / Bridal Falls RV Resort, 53480 Bridal Falls Road, is bare-land strata: freehold strata lots zoned CD-1, serviced with gas, hydro, water and sewer, with concrete pads, for full-time or lock-and-go use. A typical lot is 40 × 58 feet, and the zoning allows a cottage home or a newer RV. Amenities include a clubhouse, outdoor pool, hot tub, fitness centre and tennis courts. Because it's freehold strata, there's no pad rent; the Strata Property Act applies, not the manufactured-home park rules.
Strata block (the bare-land strata at 53: Strata rules for the bare-land strata at 53480 Bridal Falls Road: the Form B package (fees, amounts owing, special levies, contingency reserve balance, insurance, rules, budget, rental disclosure and depreciation report) sets out the fees and registered rules, and must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. With a clubhouse, pool and serviced lots, the depreciation report (required every 5 years since July 1, 2024) is especially important. At least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve, rental bans are void, and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.
Parks: Cheam Lake Wetlands Regional Park: Parks: Cheam Lake Wetlands Regional Park is a 107-hectare Fraser Valley Regional District park at 53480 Elgey Road, Rosedale, where 184 bird species have been recorded. Pets aren't allowed.
Governing bylaws: Official Community Pla: Bylaws: Official Community Plan Bylaw 1501, Zoning Bylaw 1638 (2021) and Floodplain Management Bylaw No. 1669 (2022).
Menno Place campus — Marshall Rd / Primr: Menno Place, around Marshall Road and Primrose Street, is a Mennonite Benevolent Society care campus: Menno Home (32910 Brundige Avenue) and Menno Hospital (32945 Marshall Road) are residential care homes; Menno Assisted Living (2021 Primrose Street) and Terrace East (2099 Primrose Street) are assisted living; and Menno Pavilion and Primrose Gardens (2099 Primrose Street) are independent supportive living apartments. None of it is strata ownership: the supportive-living homes are rentals, and the care homes admit through the health system.
Schools are SD34; School Locator checks: Schools are in SD34. For example, 33130 Bevan Avenue is in the catchment for Godson Elementary, Abbotsford Middle and Abbotsford Senior Secondary, and 32161 Dormick Avenue for Dormick Park Elementary, Abbotsford Middle and Abbotsford Senior Secondary. Catchments are set by address, so check the exact address.
Two neighbourhood plans steer what gets: Two neighbourhood plans guide what gets built around the 55+ buildings: the City Centre Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2913-2019) and the Historic Downtown Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2920-2019), under the Abbotsforward 2050 OCP. The OCP calls for a new mixed-use centre between the hospital and Mill Lake Park, and a primary transit corridor on South Fraser Way between Clearbrook and McCallum Road, where most of these 55+ buildings are.
Two of the \"Central Abbotsford\" names: Two buildings people search for as "Central Abbotsford" aren't clearly in this area. Central Heights Manor on King Road is often labelled Central Abbotsford but is in Poplar, and Parkside Place on Murray Avenue is listed as Central in the building directory but West in some listings. Area labels in listings are inconsistent, so use the strata plan number to identify a building (Parkside Place is LMS118, Horizon Place NWS2684, Oakhurst Park NWS1894).
Cloud Croft Manor's build year disagrees: Cloud Croft Manor is listed as built in 1976 in directories and 1975 in MLS® listings. Either way, it's a small 18-unit building from the mid-1970s and the oldest known 55+ strata in the area; the depreciation report and Form B show the year the strata uses.
From listing sources: Cloud Croft Manor: From listings: Cloud Croft Manor allows one lap-sized dog or two cats; Willband Creek Estates is described as pet friendly; Parkside Place allows one cat and no dogs; and Regency Park Tower 2 allows no pets. Listings disagree on Summerset Place, so check its bylaws.
Two 5-storey mixed-use buildings by Parc: Montvue: two mixed-use buildings by Parcel7 Homes, with homes above ground-floor shops, completed in 2025. The architect, Keystone Architecture, describes 5 storeys and 90 homes; presale directories say 6 storeys, 110 condos and 10 shops. Check the actual unit count with the strata.
Where the condo stock concentrates: (1): The condos are in three areas: along Gladwin Road and Mill Lake south of South Fraser Way, where the towers and low-rises are (Mahogany, Regency Park and Natura); Historic Downtown around Montrose Avenue, South Fraser Way and the Rail District between Pine Street and Morey Avenue (Montvue, The Mason and Upper Montrose); and the McCallum Road and King Road edge by the University of the Fraser Valley (College Park).
The fee split between the operating fund: The Form B shows how the strata fee is split between the operating fund and the contingency reserve, and the current reserve balance. Since November 1, 2023, at least 10% of the operating budget must go into the reserve.
Lot character: RS3 minimum interior lot: Lot sizes: RS3 has a minimum interior lot of 540 m², RS5 420 m², and RS7 (infill residential) 300 m² for new interior lots, with a minimum width of 10 m and depth of 22.5 m, among the smallest in the city. RS3-i (infill) zoning is used on Maple Street in the Historic Downtown plan area.
SSMUH / added units on a lot: the bylaw': Adding units: Abbotsford's small-scale housing rules allow 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 on larger lots, under conditions, and one secondary suite is allowed in any single detached house. A suite must be under 50% of the main home, and a coach house or garden suite can be up to 15% of the lot, to a maximum of 100 m². In the core, an older house's price often reflects how many units the lot allows, so check the conditions for that specific lot before paying for that potential.
If a lot were bare-land strata (no known: If a lot were bare-land strata (I don't know of any in the core), strata rules would apply: check the Form B (fee, approved levies, contingency reserve and insurance; provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page) and the depreciation report. At least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve, rental bans are void, and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older.
Where the mobile-home stock in this sub-: The area's one mobile home park, Georgian Park, is on Horn Street at the east edge of the City Centre plan area.
The usual duplex form: Zoning Bylaw 2400: Lot sizes under Zoning Bylaw 2400-2014: RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m², RS5 420 m², and RS7 (infill residential) 300 m² for new interior lots, with a minimum width of 10 m and depth of 22.5 m. RS3-i (infill) zoning is used on Maple Street in the Historic Downtown plan area.
Usually its unit potential: s.140 allows: Usually how many units it allows: 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 on larger lots, under conditions, plus one secondary suite in any single detached house. Larger forms are set by the plan designations (Urban 2 – ground oriented; Urban 1 – mid-rise up to 6 storeys). Confirm the lot's zone and designation before paying for that potential.
Enter the primary home address into the: Enter your home address in the SD34 School Locator; the district says it determines your catchment school, and registration starts there. For example, 33130 Bevan Avenue is in the catchment for Godson Elementary, Abbotsford Middle and Abbotsford Senior Secondary, and 32161 Dormick Avenue for Dormick Park Elementary, Abbotsford Middle and Abbotsford Senior Secondary.
Transit: BC Transit's service-improvemen: Transit: from January 4, 2026, BC Transit's Route 57 Broadway moved from Carleton Street one block east to McNaught Road, with new stops on McNaught and Acorn, and Sunday evening service was added on routes 57, 53 Fairfield and 51. Route 66 Fraser Valley Express runs daily between Chilliwack, Abbotsford, Langley and Burnaby.
Agriculture context for this sub-area's: Farming is big here: the City says agriculture covers 67% of Chilliwack's land and 29% of its economic activity. Check each property's Agricultural Land Reserve status.
Accessory dwelling units: Section 4.06(1: Secondary units: only one is allowed per lot where the zone permits one: a secondary suite, coach house or garden suite. Garden suites can be up to 100 m². Parking: 1 space for a one-bedroom unit or any secondary suite, and 2 for a coach house or garden suite with two or more bedrooms.
ALR housing frame, for parcels at this s: On ALR land at the east edge, a property can have one main house of up to 500 m² plus at most one additional home of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (larger parcels). Check each property's ALR status.
The in-area ladder runs: independent str: Options here range from strata ownership (Ivy Green, Spadina Regency), to subsidized independent rentals (Jubilee Place, 45440 Hodgins Avenue, 36 units for low-income people 55+, with a focus on veterans; The Paramount, 46187 Yale Road, income-tested for 65+), to retirement rentals near the hospital (Chartwell Birchwood on Patten Avenue, Chartwell Hampton House at 45555 Hodgins Avenue, and Chartwell Lynnwood at 9168 Corbould Street), to registered assisted living (Birchwood and The Cascades, 45586 McIntosh Drive). All are within a few blocks of Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Road.
One age-restricted strata building: Moun: One age-restricted strata building: Mountainview Estates, 46966 Yale Road, built around 1988–1989. Listings say 55+ and no pets, and its directory lists age restrictions. A second building on Margaret Avenue isn't clearly 55+; see the next question.
Chilliwack's ground-oriented 55+ stock i: Chilliwack's 55+ townhomes are scattered: on Young Road south of Highway 1, Patten Avenue in Chilliwack Proper, and Chehalis Drive in Sardis.
Smaller rural parcels exist in the small: Smaller rural properties exist in the small-lot farm zones: a City study gives minimums of 2 ha for AS (agriculture small lot) and 1 ha for AR (agriculture residential, with Agricultural Land Commission approval for a homesite severance). Check the current figures in Zoning Bylaw No. 5000.
Low-rise strata, Apartment/Condo sub-typ: A low-rise condo building in Chilliwack Downtown, built around 1979–1980, professionally managed, with heat and hot water included in the fee. Listings describe it as "rental-friendly (no age restrictions), No Pets". It's on the same Spadina street as two 55+ buildings, but with the opposite rules.
Apartment form confirmed by listings and: A condo building (strata plan BCS3330) in Chilliwack Downtown, built 2008–2009, with secure underground parking and in-suite laundry.
Downtown's condo stock splits into two p: Downtown's condos are in two separate pockets. The three Spadina buildings near the hospital date from the 1980s and 1990s; the Birch, Chesterfield and Cheam buildings (9000 and 9060 Birch, The Willows and Magnolia Manor), near Five Corners and District 1881, date from the 2000s. Fees, construction and warranty history differ by pocket.
Minimum lot areas inside Section 6, zone: Minimum lot sizes for creating new lots in Chilliwack's farm zones depend on how the lot is approved. AL and AU: 7.5 ha for land excluded from the ALR or an approved ALR subdivision, 1 ha by boundary adjustment, and 0.2 ha by an ALC-approved homesite severance or boundary adjustment. AS: 2 ha for an approved ALR subdivision, 1 ha by boundary adjustment, and 0.2 ha by ALC-approved severance or adjustment, or on exempt land with community water. AR: 0.2 ha with community water, otherwise 1 ha. AC: 2 ha, 1 ha by boundary adjustment with community water, and 0.2 ha by ALC-approved severance. AFP: 0.4 ha. Minimum lot width is 25 m in all six zones. These are minimums for new lots, not the size of existing farms.
Farm Home Plate figures inside Section 6: Farm home plate rules: in the AL, AR and AC zones, the area used for homes is capped at 4,000 m² for the main house and 1,000 m² for an additional home. The house must be within 70 m of the front or side lot line (with the whole home plate within 80 m), or within 50 m of the rear lot line (within 60 m). These rules don't apply to lots under 0.8 ha, and the AU, AS and AFP zones have no home plate limit. If a property doesn't meet the rules, it needs a development permit.
Age-restricted 55+ manufactured-home par: A 55+ manufactured-home park with 143 homes, a clubhouse and 1 pet allowed, on leased First Nations land. Listings say the lease runs to 2076 with an option to extend. It isn't strata: you buy the home and pay a monthly pad fee, but you don't own the land. Check the lease and tenancy documents before relying on the lease details.
Assignment on a sale needs park consent:: Selling needs the park's consent. Under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, you can assign or sublet your site only with the landlord's written consent (or a director's order, or permission in the tenancy agreement). The landlord can only refuse in specific cases and can't charge for considering or giving consent. Consent is requested on the RTB-10 form, and the seller must give the buyer the written tenancy agreement and park rules.
For contrast — the strata rules that do: For comparison, strata rules don't apply in a pad-rent park. In a strata, the only legal age bylaw is 55 and older, and it limits who can live in a home, not who can own it, with exemptions for existing residents, live-in caregivers and, since May 1, 2023, a younger spouse or partner and some children. Rental bans have been void since November 24, 2022, though short-term rental limits are still allowed. None of these exemptions automatically apply in a park, so read the park rules instead.
City frame: no manufactured-home-park zo: City rules: Chilliwack's small-scale housing amendment (Bylaw 5395, adopted June 18, 2024) allows 3 to 4 units on lots zoned for houses and duplexes inside the urban growth boundary. A secondary suite can be up to 90 m² or 40% of the home, whichever is smaller; only one secondary unit is allowed per lot; and garden suites can be up to 100 m².
Strata vs fee-simple — the core distinct: Strata or fee simple: four of the five complexes are strata. A strata townhouse buyer owns a strata lot, pays strata fees and gets a Form B package. A fee-simple townhouse buyer owns the lot outright, with no strata, Form B or strata fees; City rules and any registered covenants or homeowners' association apply.
Lot character from the hillside zones, a: Minimum lot sizes on the hillside (Zoning Bylaw No. 5000): Hillside Residential (HR) is 0.2 ha with community water or 0.4 ha otherwise, with a 25 m minimum width; Rural Hillside (RH) is 8 ha and 25 m wide; Suburban Hillside Residential (SHR) depends on the slope, from 360 m² on the gentlest to 990 m² on the steepest; and Suburban Residential (SR) is 650 m² with city water and sewer, 17.5 m wide. These are minimums, not the size of every lot.
Everything else is down the hill: no Cit: Everything else is down the hill: there's no leisure centre, library, shopping centre or grocery store on the mountain. The nearest are Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre (9145 Corbould Street), Chilliwack Library (45860 First Avenue) and Save-On-Foods Sardis (6014 Vedder Road). Chilliwack General Hospital is at 45600 Menholm Road, and the urgent and primary care centre is at #104–7955 Evans Road. People buy on the mountain for slope, views and trails, and drive for everything else.
Westpointe's own sources disagree on its: Westpointe was built around 2003–2004: a current listing says 2003, and a neighbourhood source says 2004, with 34 rancher townhomes.
Mountain-specific lot minimums differ by: Minimum lot sizes on the mountain depend on the zone and slope: Hillside Residential (HR) is 0.2 ha with community water or 0.4 ha otherwise; Rural Hillside (RH) is 8 ha; Suburban Hillside Residential (SHR) ranges from 360 m² on the gentlest slopes to 990 m² on the steepest; and Suburban Residential (SR) starts at 650 m² with full services.
Chilliwack frame in full: Official Commu: Chilliwack's plans: the Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 5500, "Chilliwack 2050") includes the Agricultural Area Plan and neighbourhood plans for Chilliwack Proper, Downtown, the Eastern Hillsides and Sardis, plus a farm home plate development permit area. The small-scale housing amendment (Bylaw No. 5395, June 18, 2024) applies in urban areas; farm properties follow the farm zones and ALR rules.
Apartment/Condo form confirmed by curren: Mountainview Estates is a freehold strata condo building in Chilliwack Proper East, built around 1988–1989. Listings describe a 55+ community ("IMMACULATE 55 + Mountainview Estates") with an amenity room, recreation centre and workshop, and no pets. The directory lists age restrictions, no pets and no rentals, though rental bans have been void since November 24, 2022.
Market context: none stated. Chilliwack: There are no market figures for this area. Chilliwack is part of the Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board, which publishes only board-wide statistics, with no figures for individual areas or for land.
Transit: BC Transit's service changes ef: Transit: from January 4, 2026, BC Transit's Route 57 Broadway moved from Carleton Street one block east to McNaught Road, with new stops on McNaught and Acorn, and Sunday evening service was added on routes 51, 53 Fairfield and 57. Route 66 Fraser Valley Express runs daily between Chilliwack, Abbotsford, Langley and Burnaby.
ALR block (provincial frame, for any ALR: For any Agricultural Land Reserve property at the edge of the area: subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, homes can't be stratified, the main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, and one additional home can be up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² on larger ones.
Apartment/Condo building labelled Chilli: The Elliot, 45562 Airport Road, by Redekop Faye: a wood-frame condo building with fibre-cement and stone siding, underground parking and a rooftop patio, built around 2020–2021 and sold out. Planning identity: the City's Official C: Fairfield Island is part of the City's Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhood Plan (Schedule B2 of the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 5500). Provincial dates that changed a bare-lan: Rule changes that affect bare-land strata lots here: rental bans void from November 24, 2022; more 55+ exemptions from May 1, 2023; at least 10% of the budget into the reserve from November 1, 2023; depreciation reports every five years from July 1, 2024; and Chilliwack's small-scale housing bylaw (5395) adopted June 18, 2024.
Chilliwack property taxes (city ground o: Chilliwack property taxes: notices are mailed at the end of May and taxes are due the first working day after July 1. A 5% penalty applied to 2026 taxes unpaid after July 2, 2026, and another 5% to taxes unpaid after August 4, 2026. Fairfield Island is inside the City of Chilliwack, so the regional district's rural tax dates (October 31) don't apply.
Bare-land strata — its own form, documen: Bare-land strata: some detached houses on Fairfield Island are on bare-land strata lots. A listing line saying "no other restrictions" isn't the strata's registered bylaws; read those in the Form B.
ALR block — full form (the northern/east: On the Agricultural Land Reserve land at the north and east edges: subdividing, a new house, coach house or suite, fill or soil removal, and non-farm uses may need Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR homes can't be stratified. The main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, plus one additional home of up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² on larger ones. Homes must also meet the City's farm home plate rules, or need a development permit. For farm tax status, you need farm income of $10,000 on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, or $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha on larger properties, with applications due by October 31. Check a property's ALR status on the City's Webmap.
Within the city-wide rules: a secondary: Suites and secondary units (Zoning Bylaw No. 5000): a secondary suite can be up to 90 m² or 40% of the home, whichever is smaller; one secondary unit is allowed per lot; and garden suites can be up to 100 m². The small-scale housing amendment (Bylaw 5395, adopted June 18, 2024) allows more units on eligible lots. Check a specific lot with the City.
If one lists, check title first: A strat: If a half duplex comes up, check the title first: a strata half comes with a Form B for its two-lot strata, while a fee-simple half is its own lot with registered party-wall agreements. I don't know of either on the island today.
A waterfront apartment-condo building: c: A waterfront condo building: listings show units built in 2023 and market it as one of the village's few buildings that allow short-term rentals, with some units run as Airbnbs. A vacation-rental source describes it as a boutique 28-unit building completed in 2024. Sources disagree on short-term rentals: listings and one industry page say they're allowed, but the same publisher's buying guide says they're prohibited. Check the strata bylaws.
An established lakefront condo building: An established lakefront condo building, described by a vacation-rental source as one of the few Esplanade buildings whose strata allows short-term rentals. A current listing shows a unit built in 1979, with no pets allowed for that unit. The same source calls the building "1980s-era"; the listing's 1979 date is used here.
Where condo stock concentrates: the Espl: The condos are on Esplanade Avenue: every known condo building is there (120, 328, 378, 450 and 470 Esplanade), and the one known townhouse complex is on Hot Springs Road (520). The 2021 Census shows how few apartments there are: of 885 occupied homes, 575 (65.0%) were detached houses, 135 (15.3%) apartments in buildings under five storeys, 100 (11.3%) row houses, and none in buildings of five or more storeys.
Short-term rentals — three layers, all l: Short-term rentals follow Village rules: Harrison Hot Springs is a designated resort region, so the provincial principal-residence rule doesn't apply. Instead, you need (1) Tourist Accommodation zoning under Bylaw No. 1115 (2017); (2) since December 15, 2025, a separate business licence for each unit under Business Licence Bylaw No. 1128 (amended by Bylaw No. 1231, 2025); and (3) a strata that allows it. Accommodation in Harrison Hot Springs, the District of Kent and FVRD Area C also pays the 3% hotel tax (MRDT), whose current term runs to January 1, 2027; check it has been renewed before counting on rental income past then.
Tenure is therefore carried as strata on: The building is a strata on a registered EPS plan; the Form B and the strata plan are the documents to check before buying.
Board ground: Harrison Hot Springs is a: There are no market figures for Harrison Hot Springs. It's in the Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board's area, which publishes no figures for individual communities.
Population and need: 1,905 people in 202: Population and housing need: 1,905 people in 2021 (up from 1,468 in 2016), with 715 owner households (80.8%) and 165 renter households (18.6%). People 65 and older were 32% of the population. The Housing Needs Report estimates a need for 185 homes over 5 years and 637 over 20 years.
Schools (SD78 Fraser-Cascade): Harrison: Schools (SD78 Fraser-Cascade): Harrison Hot Springs Elementary (K–6), 501 Hot Springs Road, with about 100 students, is the village school; students then go to Agassiz Elementary-Secondary School (Grades 7–12) in Agassiz. The elementary building is over 75 years old and over capacity. A replacement school in a shared Village and school district "Civic Campus" is only at the concept stage: a June 15, 2026 council motion to send a revised agreement to SD78 failed, a new exploratory agreement was being discussed as of August 10, 2026, and there's no funding or timeline. Check catchments with SD78.
Short-term rentals: nightly rental runs: Short-term rentals follow Village zoning and licensing, not the provincial principal-residence rule; the Province lists the Village as an exempt resort region. Since December 15, 2025, Business Licence Bylaw No. 1128 (amended by Bylaw No. 1231, 2025) requires a separate business licence for each unit rented short term. Accommodation also pays the 3% hotel tax (MRDT, collected for Tourism Harrison), whose current five-year term (2022–2026) runs to January 1, 2027; check it has been renewed before counting on rental income past then.
Flood — the village's first diligence it: Flooding is the first thing to check in the village. The existing dike crest is 13.9 m, below the 1894 record flood of 14.1 m and the required 15.1 m. The flood construction level is 14.55 m (Bylaw No. 1179, 2022), and the 1-in-200-year lake flood level is 13.95 m. In September 2025, Council directed detailed design of a deployable waterfront dike from the pump station to Rendall Park. Miami River flooding is handled by the pump station and floodbox, upgraded in 2016 for a 200-year flow. Check a lakeshore unit's floor elevation against the flood construction level before making an offer.
Fee-simple lots: small village lots in t: Fee-simple lots: small village lots in the core grid and larger lots on the east and south edges. Detached homes and cottages are usually freehold, with no strata corporation, Form B or strata fees. I don't know of any vacant bare-land strata lots here.
Pad-tenure frame — not lot stock, not la: Manufactured-home parks are pad rentals, not land ownership: Glencoe Motel and Trailer Park (259 Hot Springs Road, 27 pads in a 2020 regional district count) and Harrison Holiday Park (973 Hot Springs Road, 12 pads).
Land shape: small village lots in the co: Lots range from small village lots in the core grid to larger parcels on the east and south edges. The Official Community Plan sees the Village Centre and lakeshore as a compact, walkable resort core around the hot springs, with the lakeshore park and walkway extended from the hot springs source in the west to the marinas in the east.
Flood rules: flood construction level 14: Flood rules: the flood construction level is 14.55 m (Bylaw No. 1179, 2022). Council minutes from April 22, 2025 put the existing dike crest at 13.9 m, below the 1894 record flood of 14.1 m and the 15.1 m provincial standard. In September 2025, Council directed detailed design of a deployable waterfront dike from the pump station to Rendall Park. Check a lot's floor elevation against the flood construction level before making an offer.
