You need (1) Tourist Accommodation zoning under Bylaw No. 1115 (2017); (2) since December 15, 2025, a separate business licence for each unit under Business Licence Bylaw No. 1128 (amended by Bylaw No. 1231, 2025); and (3) for a strata, a strata that allows it. Accommodation in the area also pays the 3% hotel tax (MRDT), whose current term runs to January 1, 2027; check it has been renewed before counting on rental income past then.
Schools: Harrison Hot Springs Elementary: Schools (SD78 Fraser-Cascade): Harrison Hot Springs Elementary (K–6), 501 Hot Springs Road, and Agassiz Elementary-Secondary (Grades 7–12). Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Maybe — three layers decide it, and none: Maybe. Three things decide it, and the provincial principal-residence rule isn't one of them, because the Village is an exempt resort region: the unit needs Tourist Accommodation zoning (Zoning Bylaw No. 1115, 2017), its own Village business licence (since December 15, 2025), and a strata that allows short-term rentals. Industry sources say Harrison On The Lake and Oasis allow them and Echo Beach allows a 7-day minimum, while the four large Esplanade buildings don't; for Oasis, the same publisher's two pages disagree. Check the registered bylaws, not a listing. The 3% hotel tax (MRDT) also applies, with renewal due January 1, 2027.
Both names appear in feed listing-card t: Both names come only from listings, not from the resort or park itself, and so do the seasonal-use limits in Everglades listings (for example, full-time use March 1 to October 31 in one listing). It depends on the parcel's government an: It depends on which government the property is under and whether it's in the ALR. In the City of Mission, a suite must be registered with the City and be inside a single detached house (no suites in townhouses or rowhomes). In regional district Area F, a suite must be inside the main house; a detached garden suite isn't allowed as a suite. On ALR land, a second home must also fit the ALR limits (one additional home of 90 m² or 186 m², depending on parcel size). Check both for the specific property before planning a second home.
City planning frame (Bench only): the Ci: City planning applies only on the Bench: the City of Mission's Official Community Plan is Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026, replacing Bylaw 6350-2025 with the same vision, land use and policies plus a Regional Context Statement. The Prairie and Island parts are in the regional district's Areas F and G, under its own plans and zoning; check the bylaw and zone for a specific lot with the regional district.
ALR housing and stratification rules: th: ALR rules: most of the inhabited Hatzic Valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve. On ALR land, a property can have one main house of up to 500 m² plus at most one additional home of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (larger), and ALR homes can't be stratified, because creating a strata counts as subdividing farmland, which needs Agricultural Land Commission permission.
Prairie (Area F) and Island (Area G): FV: Hatzic Prairie (Area F) and Hatzic Island (Area G) are under the regional district and the Province. In Area F, a suite must be inside the main house; a detached garden suite isn't allowed as a suite. Property taxes follow the rural system: the notice comes from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes and you pay the Province. Taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid on July 2 and another 5% on October 31.
MHPTA note (pad stock): where a purchase: For a manufactured home on a rented pad (Green Acres or Mission Mobile Home Park), park tenancy rules apply: pad-rent increases are capped at 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026 and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027, and selling needs the park's consent to assign the tenancy.
Fee-simple lots are the default on the B: Most lots on the Bench and the Prairie are fee simple: the Bench houses (Ferguson Avenue and Jasper Avenue, and an estate listed at 5.66 acres on Ferndale Avenue) and the Prairie acreages sell as whole parcels unless the title says otherwise, with no strata corporation, Form B or strata fees.
Not fee-simple land — Green Acres Mobile: Green Acres Mobile Park, on Shook Road at Hatzic Lake, is a pad rental, not land ownership: you own the manufactured home and rent the pad, with no strata corporation or Form B. A recent listing says "Park approval is required"; no listing mentions an age rule.
Governance, three ways: the FVRD's Elect: Hatzic falls under three governments. The regional district's housing report lists Hatzic Prairie in Area F and Hatzic Island in Area G, and says the Hatzic Valley includes the historic settlements of Hatzic Prairie, Durieu, Miracle Valley and McConnell Creek. So the Bench is in the City of Mission (City bylaws, zoning and taxes), the Prairie is in regional district Area F, and the Island is in Area G (regional district and provincial rules, rural taxes). City bylaws don't apply on the Prairie or the Island.
Board row (Bench-side community context: Market figures, September 2026: in the Hatzic board area, 20 detached homes were listed and 3 sold (15% of those listed), with no condos or townhomes. Across all of Mission, 231 detached homes were listed and 28 sold, at a median of $814,000, and 122 condos and townhomes were listed and 10 sold, at a median of $430,000. The board doesn't publish a median for Hatzic itself.
City frame (Bench only): OCP Bylaw 6405-: City rules (Bench only): the Official Community Plan is Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026; zoning is Bylaw 5949-2020; and development cost charges are under Bylaw No. 5650-2017. None of these apply to the regional district parts of Hatzic.
It depends which Hatzic: On the Bench, C: It depends which part of Hatzic. On the Bench, City registration and suite rules apply (no suites in townhouses or rowhomes). On the Prairie (Area F), a suite must be inside the main house, not a detached garden suite, and on ALR land the ALR limits also apply.
Neighbours and distances, per the OCP: t: Neighbours and distances: the nearest larger town is Agassiz in the District of Kent, about 38 km from Hemlock Valley; Mission is about 55 km west; and the Village of Harrison Hot Springs is at the south end of Harrison Lake, south of the plan area.
Where the condo stock concentrates: at t: Condos and townhomes are at the base area: the one condo building is on Enzian Way at the slopes, and the rest are townhouse-style homes and half duplexes on Edelweiss Drive, Sakwi Creek Road and Snowflake Crescent, mixed in with detached cabins and chalets.
Governance: Hemlock Valley is unincorpor: Hemlock Valley is unincorporated land in the regional district's Area C, under its Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan (November 2019). The plan area follows the Controlled Recreation Area the Province created in 2016 when it approved the Hemlock Valley All Seasons Resort Master Plan, which lets the resort developer use Crown land for the purposes in that plan. The plan divides the area into Hemlock West (the original resort community), Hemlock East and Hemlock North, each to get its own neighbourhood plan as the resort grows.
The existing resort, for scale: 4 ski li: The resort today: 4 lifts serving 146.8 hectares of ski terrain on 35 named runs on the south and southwest slopes, all on natural snow. The plan puts comfortable capacity at about 1,150 skiers and snowboarders a day, and balanced resort capacity at 1,640 guests a day.
\"Hemlock\" is a Fraser Valley Real Esta: "Hemlock" is a real estate board area name, grouped under Mission, but Hemlock Valley isn't a municipality and isn't in the City of Mission. It's unincorporated land in the regional district's Area C, under its Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan (November 2019).
Where condo stock concentrates: it barel: There are very few condos or townhomes in Hope: three strata complexes, a low-rise on Scott Drive and two townhouse complexes on Douglas Street and 7th Avenue. The District's figures show a mostly single-family market: building permits from 2021 to October 2024 were mostly for houses (70 units) plus suites (22). The townsite around Wallace Street has what apartments and townhouses there are; Silver Creek is mostly family ranchers, and Kawkawa Lake is mostly recreational properties.

Zoning is District of Hope Zoning Bylaw No. 1324 (2012), with amendments including Bylaw 1580 (2024), the small-scale multi-unit housing amendment for the RS-1 zone, adopted June 10, 2024.

Recreation and health: the Hope & Area R: Recreation and health: the Hope & Area Recreation Centre (1005 6th Avenue), run by the regional district, has an arena, the Dan Sharrers Aquatic Centre and a fitness centre. Kawkawa Lake, Memorial Park and the Coquihalla Canyon (Othello Tunnels) trails are the big outdoor draws; the tunnels park is being restored in phases after the November 2021 atmospheric river, with the northern part reopened June 27, 2025 (three of the five tunnels), so check BC Parks for current status. Fraser Canyon Hospital, 1275 7th Avenue, is a 10-bed Fraser Health hospital with 24/7 emergency care.

Pad-tenure frame — not lot stock, not la: Manufactured-home parks on the edges of the District (including Lismore Mobile Home Park, Windmill Park and Crystal River Court on Flood-Hope Road) are pad rentals or leases: you own the home, not the land.

Serviced vs unserviced ground: townsite: Services: townsite lots are on the District's water and sewer, with water, sewer and garbage fees on the tax notice (Utility Bylaw No. 1153). Don't assume a lot outside the townsite is serviced because a listing says so; check with the District.
One current listing calls a unit Row / T: One current listing calls a unit Row / Townhouse (built 1994); another calls a unit Apartment/Condo (built 1995) while describing the complex as townhouses. Check the strata plan and Form B for the specific unit.
Where condo stock concentrates: almost e: Condos and townhomes are almost all in the Agassiz townsite (around MacKay Crescent, Heath Road and Morrow Road), plus one strata pocket at Mount Woodside (Harrison Highlands, off Highlands Boulevard and Woodside Boulevard). Most of the District is freehold; strata homes are mainly townhouses in Agassiz and Mount Woodside.
District plans and zoning (District sour: Plans and zoning: the District of Kent Official Community Plan 2025 directs most growth into the Agassiz townsite, with Mount Woodside as a smaller growth village. Zoning is District of Kent Zoning Bylaw No. 1219 (2001, as amended). Bylaw No. 1737 (adopted June 10, 2024) created the RS1 zone, allowing up to four homes on single-family lots, and the District's guide says there are no RS1 properties outside Agassiz and Harrison Highlands. Secondary suites are allowed in single-family homes in all residential zones.
Board ground: the District sits in CADRE: There are no market figures for Kent. It's in the Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board's area, where it's listed as Agassiz, and the board publishes no figures for individual communities.
Riverwynd's 32 town homes rest on its de: Riverwynd's count of 32 townhomes comes from its original launch advertising.
Timberlane (1275 Scott Drive) is held ou: Timberlane (1275 Scott Drive): current listings disagree on whether it's townhouses or condos (Row / Townhouse, built 1994, in one; Apartment/Condo, built 1995, in another), though both describe townhouses.
District plan and zoning: the plan is th: Plans and zoning: the District of Kent Official Community Plan 2025 directs most growth into the Agassiz townsite, with Mount Woodside as a smaller growth village. Zoning is District of Kent Zoning Bylaw No. 1219 (2001, as amended). Bylaw No. 1737 (adopted June 10, 2024) created the RS1 zone, allowing up to four homes on single-family lots, but the District's guide says there are no RS1 properties outside Agassiz and Harrison Highlands, so rural Kent lots don't get the four-unit option. Secondary suites are allowed in single-family homes in all residential zones. The District's 2024 Interim Housing Needs Report found 495 new homes needed now and 1,695 more by 2041.
Flood, dikes and drainage — the District: Flooding, dikes and drainage: the District's flat land is Fraser and Harrison floodplain protected by dikes. The District maintains 135 km of drainage ditches and supports Fraser River gravel removal to reduce flood risk, and the Province regulates the dikes, pump stations and flood boxes, including the Hammersley Pump Station about 6 km west of Agassiz. On the flats, check flood protection; at Mount Woodside, check the steep-slope and creek-side hazard rules in the OCP.
Townsite lots sit in Agassiz; large farm: Townsite lots are in Agassiz, large farm parcels (often tens of acres) cover the plain, and mid-size lots are at Mount Woodside. Most of the District is freehold; strata homes are mainly townhouses in Agassiz and Mount Woodside.
Floodplain and slope character, by pocke: The flat land is Fraser and Harrison floodplain protected by dikes, with 135 km of District drainage ditches, while Mount Woodside has creek-side and steep-slope hazards. On the flats, check flood protection; at Mount Woodside, check the slope rules in the OCP.
Flood / diking: Flood Protection & Erosi: Flooding and dikes: the OCP's flood protection section covers this, and the Province's dike maps for Kent show the dikes, pump stations and flood boxes it regulates, including the Hammersley Pump Station about 6 km west of Agassiz.
Fee-simple farm parcels are the acreage: Acreages here are fee-simple farm parcels: no strata corporation, Form B or strata fee. District zoning, ALR rules where the parcel is in the reserve, dike and drainage obligations, and any registered covenants apply instead.
Land base and commuting frame: Highway 7: Roads and transit: Highway 7 (Lougheed) runs the length of the District, and Highway 9 connects Agassiz south across the Fraser to Chilliwack and Highway 1, and north to Harrison Hot Springs. BC Transit Route 71 (Chilliwack–Agassiz–Harrison Hot Springs) and Route 72 (Agassiz–Hope via Highway 7) serve the area, with Agassiz as the hub.
ALR farm-residence forms — only as ALR s: On ALR land, the farm housing rules apply: one main house per parcel, a suite only inside it, and one additional size-limited home for farm or another permitted use. A farm with a main house and a legal additional home sells as one property, not as a duplex, and ALR homes can't be stratified without Agricultural Land Commission permission.
The District's strata stock is townhouse: Strata homes in the District are townhouses, in the Agassiz townsite and at Mount Woodside, plus detached and semi-detached homes. If you need a condo apartment, look in Chilliwack.
Planning frame: the governing plan is th: Plans: the regional district's Electoral Area C Official Community Plan (Bylaw 1747, 2024, adopted September 18, 2025) applies, and includes a Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan. It replaced the older plan for Morris Valley, Harrison Mills and Lake Errock (Bylaw No. 0020, 1998).
Governance: Lake Errock is unincorporate: Lake Errock is unincorporated land in the regional district's Area C, whose plan area runs "from the Harrison River to the east of Deroche and includes Morris Valley, Harrison Mills, Lake Errock, and the eastern portions of the Deroche Bench." The current Area C Official Community Plan (Bylaw 1747, 2024, adopted September 18, 2025) includes a Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan and replaced the 1998 plan (Bylaw No. 0020).
Form B diligence (any strata purchase he: For any strata purchase here (Tapadera, Eagle Point or River Reach), read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. On a bare-land strata, the Form B and bylaws also show what you can put on the lot (RV, park model or manufactured home); a listing doesn't.
Local plan — FVRD, not a city: the gover: Plans are set by the regional district, not a city: the Area C Official Community Plan (Bylaw 1747, 2024, adopted September 18, 2025), including the Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan, replaced the 1998 plan. Tapadera's development guide refers to Zoning Bylaw No. 1638 (2021) for holiday park requirements. Check a specific lot's designation, permit areas and allowed homes with the regional district.
ALR frame (applies parcel by parcel): an: On ALR land: one main house of up to 500 m², a suite only inside it, and at most one additional home of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (larger). ALR homes can't be stratified, so a farm can't be turned into townhouse strata lots.
Bare-land strata — its own form, documen: Tapadera Estates, 14600 Morris Valley Road, is a bare-land strata (strata plan LMS648): you own a strata lot, with a Form B, strata fees for the common property and registered bylaws. It isn't fee simple, even if the lot has an RV, park model or manufactured home on it. Listings also describe it as part of Harrison Mills, so it shows up under both names.
Bare-land strata rules (for a Tapadera-t: Bare-land strata rules (for a lot like Tapadera's): the Form B, with the rules, budget and latest depreciation report, must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited), and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.
Tapadera Estates: A bare-land strata lot: At Tapadera Estates you own the strata lot and the home on it, pay strata fees and follow the registered bylaws; the Form B is the key document. It isn't a pad rental, and manufactured-home park rules don't apply.
ALR (parcel by parcel, only where the pa: On ALR land: subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, homes can't be stratified, the main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, and one additional home can be up to 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (larger). A manufactured home on farmland is allowed only through the ALR's specific approval routes for manufactured homes or non-farm residential use.
Both names appear in listing-card text o: Both names come only from listings, for estate-style homes on Morris Valley Road, not from a developer or strata, so I can't say whether they're strata. Check the title and any strata plan for a specific property.
No — it is Freehold Strata in single-fam: No. It's freehold strata in single-family form: detached estate homes on strata lots beside Sandpiper Golf Course (a current listing shows Single Family Residence on freehold strata title). The fee pays for strata services (grounds, management and snow removal, per the listing), and the Form B is still the key document, but the home is a house, not a townhouse.
For counts, yes: SnapStats carries a Lak: For counts, yes: the board reports Lake Errock separately, under Mission. In September 2026, 16 detached homes were listed and 1 sold (6% of those listed), and 1 condo or townhome was listed with none sold. There's no median price for Lake Errock; medians are published only for Mission as a whole, and those aren't Lake Errock's.
The Fraser Valley Regional District: its: The Fraser Valley Regional District. Its Area C Official Community Plan (Bylaw 1747, 2024, adopted September 18, 2025) covers Lake Errock and includes a Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan; it replaced the 1998 plan (Bylaw No. 0020). Regional district zoning applies lot by lot, so check a specific lot's designation, permit areas and allowed homes with the regional district.
Where condo stock concentrates: there is: There are no condo buildings. Strata homes here are three bare-land strata communities of detached cottages on Columbia Valley Road; the rest are lake cottages and cabins, many first built for summer use and since converted to year-round homes, plus newer custom lake homes along the south shore, mostly freehold.
Schools are School District 33 (Chilliwa: Schools are in SD33 (Chilliwack): Cultus Lake Community School, 71 Sunnyside Boulevard in Cultus Lake Park, is the lake's elementary school, and the district groups the Columbia Valley and Cultus Lake area as Cultus Lake Elementary, then Mount Slesse Middle, then G.W. Abbotsford's suite rule is a suite under: In Abbotsford, a suite must be under 50% of the main home, and a coach house or garden suite can be up to 15% of the lot, to a maximum of 100 m². On ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission's rules apply instead: generally one home per parcel unless it qualifies for an additional one, a main house of up to 500 m² (with no more than 1,000 m² of fill), and a suite only inside it. Anything more needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, and the City may restrict homes further. Under the Commission's current policy, an extra home beyond these rules is only allowed if it's needed for farming, such as farm-worker housing.

Parks and hazards frame: Sumas Mountain: Parks and hazards: Sumas Mountain Regional Park, 39100 Sumas Mountain Forest Service Road, has trails linking to a larger network, including the Chadsey Lake Trail from the upper parking lot, for hiking, trail running and mountain biking, open 7 a.m. to sunset. City parks on the slopes include Lower Sumas Mountain Park, McKinley Park, Glenridge Park and Eagle Mountain Park. In the McKee plan area, open space is made up of creek setbacks, critical habitat, geotechnical areas and slopes over 40%, with trails planned in the McKee Trail Strategy, and the City requires a development permit on steep slopes. There's no recreation centre or library on the mountain; Abbotsford Recreation Centre (2499 McMillan Road) is at the west foot, and the nearest hospital is Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre (32900 Marshall Road).
ALR position (east-side ground, parcel-b: ALR land on the east side: the OCP's ALR map shows an Agriculture designation on the east side of the mountain. On ALR land, subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval and homes can't be stratified (Straiton is a legal bare-land strata because it's on City land outside the ALR). The main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, plus one additional home of up to 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (larger). For farm tax status, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.
City minimum lots frame the slope stock:: Minimum lot sizes on the slopes (Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014): 0.4 hectares in Suburban Residential (SR), 2.0 hectares in Country Residential (CR) and 4.0 hectares in Rural Residential (RR).
No — School Locator checks split the mou: No, catchments split the mountain. For example, 36367 Stephen Leacock Drive is in the catchment for Auguston Traditional Elementary, Clayburn Middle and Robert Bateman Secondary, while 2540 Eagle Mountain Drive is in the catchment for Irene Kelleher Totí:ltawtxw Elementary, William A. Fraser Middle and Yale Secondary.
Flood — the defining fact of this sub-ar: Flooding is the defining fact here. After the November 2021 floods on Sumas Prairie, the Province and partners signed the Sumas River Watershed Flood Mitigation Planning Initiative in April 2023. The Province is providing $3.3 million for design and assessment work, and has provided about $220 million for recovery, preparedness and flood protection in Abbotsford and Sumas Prairie since 2021, including $76.6 million to upgrade the Barrowtown Pump Station. The Province notes that December flooding again showed how prone the area is to high water, and the studies are at various stages, so flood protection here is still being planned, not finished.
The ALC housing frame on ALR parcels: la: On ALR land: generally one home per parcel unless the owner qualifies for an additional one; the main house can be up to 500 m², with a suite only inside it; and an additional detached home can be up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² on larger ones. Check a specific Sumas Prairie property's ALR status.
ALR block (full — this is dyked-prairie: Sumas Prairie is dyked farmland. On ALR land, subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, homes can't be stratified, and there's generally one home per parcel unless the owner qualifies for an additional one. The main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, and an additional home can be up to 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (larger). Farm tax status needs farm income of $10,000 on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, or $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha, with applications due by October 31. Check a specific property's ALR status on the Agricultural Land Commission's maps.
Two frames sit together: the City's suit: Two sets of rules apply: Abbotsford's (a suite under 50% of the main home, and a coach house or garden suite up to 15% of the lot, to a maximum of 100 m²) and, on ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission's (a suite only inside the main house, and an additional detached home of 90 m² or 186 m², depending on parcel size). Check the property's ALR status and zone first.
Schools: Evans Elementary, K-5, 7600 Eva: Schools (SD33 Chilliwack): Evans Elementary (K–5), 7600 Evans Road; Vedder Middle School (6–8), 45560 South Sumas Road; and Sardis Secondary (9–12), 45460 Stevenson Road. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Provincial dates that changed this build: Rule changes that affect this building: rental bans void from November 24, 2022; an insurance summary in the Form B from April 1, 2023; at least 10% of the budget into the reserve from November 1, 2023; stratas in the regional district needing a depreciation report by July 1, 2026; and the first-time buyers' GST rebate on new homes, law since March 13, 2026.
If it is strata: Form B first: Strata Pr: If it's a strata, start with the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance, parking and storage, and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. That applies to Creekside Estates, the area's one strata building, and to any townhouse strata built here in future.
The board boundary is a trap in this sub: Watch the board boundary here. Chilliwack is part of the Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board, which publishes only board-wide figures, so a "West Chilliwack median townhouse price" quoted elsewhere doesn't come from the board. There's no townhome-only figure in any case.
Cottonwood Village — 7610 Evans Road. Pa: Cottonwood Village, 7610 Evans Road, is a manufactured-home park, not land for sale. Some listings call homes there "Townhouse" or "duplex-style townhouse", but you own the home and rent the pad on leased land, with no strata and no Form B.
Services are outside the sub-area: neare: Services are outside the area: the nearest recreation centres are Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre (Unit 1, 9145 Corbould Street) and Cheam Leisure Centre (45501 Market Way); Chilliwack Library is at 45860 First Avenue; the nearest grocery store is Save-On-Foods (46020 Yale Road); and Chilliwack General Hospital is at 45600 Menholm Road, with the urgent and primary care centre at #104-7955 Evans Road.
Services: the Chilliwack Urgent and Prim: Services: the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre is in the area at #104-7955 Evans Road, and Chilliwack General Hospital is at 45600 Menholm Road. The nearest recreation centres (Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre, 9145 Corbould Street, and Cheam Leisure Centre, 45501 Market Way), Chilliwack Library (45860 First Avenue) and the nearest grocery store (Save-On-Foods, 46020 Yale Road) are outside it.
Age rules — sources discipline: In a str: Age rules: in a strata, only a 55+ bylaw is valid. A park's marketed 45+ or 40+ age (as at Country Park Village or Rainbow Estates, which are outside this area) only holds, if at all, as a park rule, and BC's human rights rules for parks are written around age 55. Read the park's actual rules, not the marketing.
Chilliwack plan / zoning frame: OCP = Ch: Plans and zoning: the Official Community Plan is Chilliwack 2050 (Bylaw No. 5500), and this area is covered by its Agricultural Area Plan. Zoning is Bylaw No. 5000; in the AL (Agricultural Lowland) zone, new lots must be at least 7.5 ha (on land excluded from the ALR or with an approved ALR subdivision), 1 ha by boundary adjustment, or 0.2 ha by an approved homesite severance, with a 25 m minimum width. The small-scale housing bylaw (5395, adopted June 18, 2024) doesn't apply to pad rentals, and on ALR land the ALR rules apply instead. The Province's extension to December 31, 2030 for part of Chilliwack Proper and Hazel Park doesn't cover this area.
ALR BLOCK IN FULL (this sub-area is farm: The whole area is farmland. On ALR land, subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, homes can't be stratified, the main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, and one additional home can be up to 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (larger). Farm tax status needs farm income of $10,000 on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, or $2,500 plus 5% of the farm value over 4 ha, with applications due by October 31. Check a property's ALR status on the Agricultural Land Commission's maps. Floodplain setbacks (Bylaw No. 4519) are 60 m from the Fraser River, 75 m from the Vedder River, and 30 m from the Chilliwack River and Vedder Canal; the City maintains the Fraser and Vedder dikes, and drainage and dyking levies are added to property taxes.
Schools: Evans Elementary, K-5, School D: Schools (SD33 Chilliwack): Evans Elementary (K–5), 7600 Evans Road; Vedder Middle School (6–8), 45560 South Sumas Road; and Sardis Secondary (9–12), 45460 Stevenson Road. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Kent is the municipality; Agassiz is the: Kent is the municipality, and Agassiz is the townsite inside it. Schools are in SD78 Fraser-Cascade. For real estate, it's in the Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board's area, which lists it as Agassiz, not Kent.
Named developments: Spencer Estates (323: Spencer Estates (32361 McRae Avenue) is named only in listings.
Fee-simple lots are the default form: Ho: Lots are fee simple. Houses are in the urban zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019; the standard is RS-1 (Single Detached Residential), with a minimum lot of 668.0 m², 18.0 m wide and 27.0 m deep, and up to 40% lot coverage. The Albion Area Plan's residential designations include Low Density Residential (single detached, with 2,000 m² lots in the designation text), Ground-Oriented Residential, Cluster Residential and Townhouse, plus an Albion Village Commercial area.
Main roads and commute: Lougheed Highway: Main roads: Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) along the south side; 240 Street, the main north–south road; and 102 Avenue and 104 Avenue running east–west through the neighbourhood. The Golden Ears Bridge, west of the city, connects Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows to Langley and Surrey.
Schools physically in the area : Albion: Schools in the area: Albion Elementary, 10031 240 Street; c'usqunela Elementary, 24093 104 Avenue; Kanaka Creek Elementary, 11120 234A Street (at the west edge); and Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary, 10445 245 Street. BC strata rules — apply in full to any s: BC strata rules apply to any strata home here, including resales in the four townhome complexes: the Form B must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page; stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years; at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve; rental bans are void; and only 55+ age bylaws are valid, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable. None of the four complexes is 55+, and I don't know of any 55+ strata townhouses in Maple Ridge. At The Warwick, find out first whether the unit is a developer sale or a resale, because the documents differ (disclosure statement and GST, or Form B).
Serviced vs unserviced ground: the urban: Services: the urban core is on City services; on the South Albion farm edge, services vary by property, so check each one.

Both homes are on one title; it isn't a duplex.
Where the condo stock concentrates: ther: There are no condo buildings in Albion. The strata homes are townhouse complexes along 240 Street between 101 and 104 Avenue: Albion Station (10151 240 Street), Ridgemont (24108 104 Avenue) and The Warwick (10392 240A Street), beside the Albion shopping corner at 104 Avenue and 240 Street.
Form B diligence (all four counted compl: All four complexes are strata, so read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. At The Warwick, find out first whether the unit is a developer sale or a resale, because the documents differ.
Schools: Albion Elementary, K-7, School: Schools (SD42 Maple Ridge–Pitt Meadows): Albion Elementary (K–7), 10031 240 Street; c'usqunela Elementary (K–7), 24093 104 Avenue; and Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary (8–12), 10445 245 Street. The one 55+ strata ownership complex in: The one 55+ strata complex in Central Meadows: self-managed freehold strata (plan NWS2727), with ground-level rancher townhomes beside Hoffman Park. MLS® listings say "Age Restricted 55+" and allow one pet, cat or dog, with restrictions. Listings describe "just 26 homes" and a 10-minute walk to the Seniors Centre, but one listing says 20 units, and sources give 1988 or 1989 as the build year, so check before relying on the numbers.
Meadowlands Housing Co-operative — 19032: Meadowlands Housing Co-operative, 19032 Advent Road, is a 55+ co-op, not strata: you can't buy a home there. The co-op calls itself a "vibrant 55+ community" beside Hoffman Park, with 16 four-unit single-storey row-home buildings (64 homes: 32 for one person and 32 for two), an activity centre and on-site maintenance. The Co-operative Housing Federation of BC says: "All units are designated for adults 55 years and up only. One indoor cat is permitted." Members buy co-op shares and pay a monthly housing charge; apply directly to the co-op.
The Wesbrooke — 12000 190A Street: A sen: The Wesbrooke, 12000 190A Street, is a seniors community with independent and assisted living, certified nurses and 24-hour staff, a workout room and a hair salon, registered with BC's Assisted Living Registry (operator Casa Living Inc.). A 2023 City staff report describes it as "a retirement home and senior's centre… offers senior residents independent living," completed in 2011. Older advertising described "a registered 33 suite assisted living residence" and all-inclusive rental suites from junior studios to two-bedrooms. It's rental and care only, with nothing for sale.
City zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 2505, 2011: Zoning (Bylaw No. 2505, 2011): houses are in the RS Large Lot Residential and R-3, R-4 and R-6 Urban Residential zones. R-3 allows up to 3 units per lot, R-4 up to 4, and R-6 up to 5, or 6 near frequent transit if at least one unit meets the BC Building Code's adaptable housing standard. The 1,215 m² minimum lot area in those zones applies only to new lots, not to building on existing lots.
One complex: Meadowland Village, 18960 A: One complex: Meadowland Village, 18960 Advent Road, ground-level rancher townhomes in a self-managed freehold strata (plan NWS2727), listed as "Age Restricted 55+". No other strata in the area has an age restriction.
Floodplain: the City's 2020 Business Pla: Floodplain: the City says over 95% of Pitt Meadows is on the Fraser and Pitt river floodplain, protected by 60 km of dikes; this area is in drainage Area 3 (Kennedy, including McKechnie). An older City release said about 86%, so check a specific property with the City.
Civic core: Pitt Meadows Family Recreati: Civic core: Pitt Meadows Family Recreation Centre (12027 Harris Road), Pitt Meadows Public Library (200-12099 Harris Road), sxwhekwnes (Spirit Square, 11985 Harris Road) and Harris Road Park by Lougheed Highway. Shopping: Meadowvale Shopping Centre (Save-On-Foods) in the Harris Road North area, and Meadowtown Shopping Centre (19800 Lougheed Highway, Real Canadian Superstore) at the northeast edge. The nearest hospital is Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, Maple Ridge.
Parks, recreation and library: sxwhekwne: Parks, recreation and library: sxwhekwnes (Spirit Square, 11985 Harris Road) is in the civic centre near City Hall; Harris Road Park by Lougheed Highway serves the north end; Pitt Meadows Family Recreation Centre is at 12027 Harris Road; and Pitt Meadows Public Library, the city's only library, is at 200-12099 Harris Road.
Zoning / OCP — Pitt Meadows frame: Zonin: Zoning and plans: under Zoning Bylaw No. 2505 (2011), houses are in the RS Large Lot Residential and R-3, R-4 and R-6 Urban Residential zones. R-3 allows up to 3 units per lot, R-4 up to 4, and R-6 up to 5, or 6 near frequent transit if at least one unit meets the BC Building Code's adaptable housing standard; the 1,215 m² minimum lot area applies only to new lots. The Official Community Plan, "I See Pitt Meadows 2040" (Bylaw No. 2864, 2020, adopted September 27, 2022), designates this area as the Municipal Town Centre.
Floodplain: The city is almost entirely: Floodplain: the city is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes, and Central Meadows is in drainage Area 3 (Kennedy, including McKechnie). The floodplain bylaw (No. 2384, 2008) sets the flood construction level at the designated flood level plus 0.6 metres; for a manufactured home, the ground or pad must be at least that high.
A mixed-use project of four buildings, f: A mixed-use project of four buildings, with four storeys of homes over ground-floor shops and "200+ condominiums" in total, according to presale marketing. Listings give the building addresses and years: 22633 Selkirk Avenue (2024), 11865 227 Street (2022), 11893 227 Street (2019) and 22638 119 Avenue (2020).

ALR rules (carried for any parcel where: For any property in the Agricultural Land Reserve (check the Agricultural Land Commission's maps): subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR homes can't be stratified. The main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an additional home can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha).
Co-op age rules are membership rules, no: Co-op age rules are membership rules, not strata bylaws: St. George's Village requires members to be 55 or older (a dependant 19 or older can live with a member), according to its application form. In a co-op, the members jointly own the housing, buy shares and help run it.
The sub-area's only 55+ ownership comple: The area's only 55+ ownership option, St. George's Village, owns its land outright, according to its application form. That's worth confirming when you buy a share, because many co-ops are on leased land.
Transit: the bus route named for the are: Transit: bus 745 Haney Place / Cottonwood serves the area, and the 746 Haney Place / Albion links with it at Jackson Road and 103 Avenue to form one loop. There's no West Coast Express station in Cottonwood.
Strata vs fee-simple — the core distinct: Strata or fee simple: three of the complexes are strata (The Meadows, Cottonwood Terrace and Carriage Lane). A strata townhouse buyer owns a strata lot, pays strata fees and gets a Form B. A fee-simple townhouse buyer owns the lot outright, with no strata, Form B or strata fees; City rules and any registered covenants or homeowners' association apply.
Form B diligence (strata complexes): Str: For the strata complexes, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
What is settled: no Cottonwood-specific: There's no area plan for Cottonwood, so the Official Community Plan's general policies apply. Nearby, the Albion Area Plan was adopted October 28, 2025 (Albion is east of 240 Street, outside Cottonwood), and the Lougheed Transit Corridor plan to the south, which ends at 221 Street, was adopted January 27, 2026.
The stock: no Cottonwood area plan exist: There's no Cottonwood area plan, so City-wide housing rules apply. The streets around the two elementary schools are single-detached subdivisions in the RS zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019. Homes are mostly freehold houses, with secondary suites and the small-scale housing rules as the ways to add units. Fee simple means your own title, with no strata, Form B or strata fees.
Tenure trap on the area's edge — not lan: At the north edge, St. George's Village Seniors Housing Co-operative (23580 Dewdney Trunk Road) is a co-op: its membership form says the co-op "has clear title to land", and members buy shares, not lots.
Land assemblies / development sites / re: I don't know of any land assemblies, development sites or rezoning proposals in Cottonwood. To the south, the Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan directs growth around future rapid bus stations along Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road; that's a plan for the corridor, not lots for sale in Cottonwood.
Transit: the bus route named for this ar: Transit: bus 745 Haney Place / Cottonwood serves the area, and the 746 Haney Place / Albion links with it at Jackson Road and 103 Avenue to form one loop. There's no West Coast Express station in Cottonwood; the nearest are in the Town Centre.
Suites and added units: one secondary su: Suites and extra units: one secondary suite per lot, inside the house, up to 40% of its floor area, not in the floodplain area, with a building permit. Eligible single-detached and duplex lots can have up to three, four or six units under the City's small-scale housing rules, subject to zoning and building code requirements. For a Cottonwood house, the value question is a suite or extra units, not subdividing, and because suites aren't allowed in the floodplain, check the City's flood map.
Schools: Kanaka Creek Elementary, K-7, S: Schools (SD42 Maple Ridge–Pitt Meadows): Kanaka Creek Elementary (K–7), 11120 234A Street; Alexander Robinson Elementary (K–7), 11849 238B Street; and Thomas Haney Secondary (7–12), 23000 116 Avenue. Freehold strata, built 1991 (building so: Freehold strata, built in 1991 (one MLS® listing says 1990). Chartwell Willow Retirement Community —: Chartwell Willow Retirement Community, 12275 224 Street: independent living, assisted living and private long-term care in one building in central Maple Ridge. Suites range from studios to two-bedrooms and are pet friendly. It's rental and care only, with nothing to buy.
Maple Ridge Towers — 11929 222 St: and M: Maple Ridge Towers (11929 222 Street) and Maple Towers (11841 222 Street) are subsidized seniors rentals, run by the Maple Ridge Elderly Citizens Society / Affordable Housing Societies and by Baptist Housing Society of B.C., with income-based rent. 222 Street is the west edge of the area.
City zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019;: City zoning (Bylaw No. 7600-2019) and the Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 7060-2014): houses are mostly RS-1, with a minimum lot of 668.0 m², 18.0 m wide and 27.0 m deep, and up to 40% coverage. Town Centre properties have commercial, multi-family and comprehensive development zones under the same bylaw.
The Town Centre plan quietly governs the: The Town Centre plan covers the downtown half of this area. There's no City plan called "East Central"; the downtown part of this board area is in the City's Town Centre Area Plan, whose boundaries were expanded to include River Bend.
Schools: Eric Langton Elementary, K-7, S: Schools (SD42 Maple Ridge–Pitt Meadows): Eric Langton Elementary (K–7), 12138 Edge Street; Golden Ears Elementary (K–7), 23124 118 Avenue; and District 42 Alternative Secondary (9–12), 23125 116 Avenue. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Building by building: The Willows' listi: Building by building: The Willows' listing allows 2 cats, 2 dogs or 1 of each; the Alouette park listing says no dogs and one indoor cat only; and Chartwell Willow (rental) is pet friendly. Check the bylaws or park rules for the specific home.
A mixed-use project of four buildings wi: A mixed-use project of four buildings, with four storeys of homes over ground-floor shops and "200+ condominiums" in total, according to presale marketing; Phase 3 alone was marketed at 44 condos. Listings give the building addresses and years: 22633 Selkirk Avenue (2024, marketed as "Brickwater 4"), 11865 227 Street (2022), 11893 227 Street (2019) and 22638 119 Avenue (2020).
Where the condo stock concentrates, in t: The condos are in two clusters: the Fraserview Village 55+ buildings on and around 116 Avenue and 225–227 Streets (Rosewood Court, Emerald Manor, The Willows, Castlemount and Riverside), and the downtown Haney buildings along Fraser Street and 227 Street, including Brickwater and the new Podium and Highpointe buildings.
Where the townhouse stock actually sits:: The townhouses are along the 116 Avenue corridor south of downtown (Fraser Glen at 22740, Dogwood Lane at 22555 and Duet at 22977), plus Gold Creek Estates on 228 Street and Alouette Estates at the east edge on 232 Street. The condos are in the Town Centre along 224, 226 and 227 Streets and 121 Avenue.
That figure COMBINES condos and townhome: That figure combines condos and townhomes; there's no townhome-only figure. Maple Ridge's median for condos and townhomes was $525,000 in September 2026, and there's no median for this area alone.
The Town Centre Area Plan (OCP s. 10.4): The Town Centre Area Plan covers the west end. Its update added River Bend, simplified the land use designations and added a Town Centre Core designation allowing higher density around the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station, both of which are transit-oriented areas under Bylaw No. 8001-2024.
The newest seniors stock downtown is not: The newest buildings downtown aren't seniors housing, and the 55+ stratas date from the 1990s: the Town Centre's recent growth (Podium, Brickwater, Highpointe and the transit-oriented areas) is for the general market.
The village buildings share one amenity: The village buildings share one amenity building with an indoor pool, hot tub, exercise room or clubhouse, and guest suite. Listings for The Willows say the fee includes the amenity building and gas, and Rosewood Court and Emerald Manor listings say gas and hot water are included. What's included differs by building, so check the Form B.
Schools: Eric Langton Elementary, K-7, S: Schools: Eric Langton Elementary (K–7, SD42), 12138 Edge Street; Harry Hooge Elementary (K–7, SD42), 12280 230 Street; and St. Patrick's (K–7, independent), 22589 121 Avenue. Bare-land strata: present only as a scat: Bare-land strata: there are a few scattered lots, but no named community. On a bare-land strata lot, you own a strata lot, pay strata fees and follow the bylaws, and the Form B is the key document.
Main roads: Lougheed Highway (Highway 7): Main roads: Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) along the south side; Dewdney Trunk Road east–west through downtown and the neighbourhoods to the east; 224 Street and 226 Street north–south through the downtown core; and the Haney Bypass, linking Lougheed Highway to Port Haney at the southwest corner.
Transit anchors: Haney Place Exchange is: Transit: Haney Place Exchange is in this area, served by routes including the R3, 701, 733, 741, 743, 744, 745, 746, 748, 749 and 791. Civic anchors: Maple Ridge Leisure Centr: Civic centre: Maple Ridge Leisure Centre (11925 Haney Place); Memorial Peace Park on 224 Street between Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road, surrounded by City Hall, the Greg Moore Youth Centre, The ACT Arts Centre and Haney Place Mall, with the Cenotaph, bandstand and Haney Farmers Market; Maple Ridge Public Library (130–22470 Dewdney Trunk Road), the city's only library; and Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre in Haney Place Mall (121–11900 Haney Place, open 7 days, 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.). Market thinness: SnapStats has no land c: There are no separate figures for land: the board reports detached homes and condos and townhomes only. Maple Ridge's medians that month were $1,131,000 for detached homes and $525,000 for condos and townhomes.
Town Centre Core / River Bend (plan desi: Town Centre Core and River Bend are plan designations, not sites for sale. The Town Centre Area Plan update added River Bend, simplified the land use designations and added a Town Centre Core designation allowing higher density downtown around the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station, both transit-oriented areas under Bylaw No. 8001-2024. The City publishes no boundary for the M: The City doesn't publish a boundary for the board's "East Central" area. Lougheed Transit Corridor — adopted Jan: The Lougheed Transit Corridor plan was adopted January 27, 2026 (Official Community Plan Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021, after a public hearing on January 20). The corridor runs along Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road from the city's west boundary to the Town Centre at 221 Street.
SSMUH / suites / subdivision potential a: Suites and extra units: one secondary suite per lot, inside the house, up to 40% of its floor area, and not in the floodplain area. Eligible single-family and duplex lots can have up to three, four or six units under the City's small-scale housing rules. Subdividing an RS-1 lot still needs the minimum 668.0 m² lot, 18.0 m wide and 27.0 m deep; extra units don't create new lots.
Bare-land strata rules (where a bare-lan: On a bare-land strata lot, BC strata rules apply: check the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page). Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited by bylaw), and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, with exemptions for a younger spouse or partner, caregivers, existing residents and some children, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.
ALR rules (for completeness — no ALR gro: I don't know of any ALR land here. If there were: subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, homes can't be stratified, the main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, and an additional home can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm tax status, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.
East Central's land story is density pol: In East Central, land value comes from density policy, not vacant lots: the Town Centre Core designation, the two transit-oriented areas (Haney Place Exchange and Port Haney Station), the Lougheed Transit Corridor (adopted January 27, 2026) and the Albion Area Plan (adopted October 28, 2025) all point to land assemblies and extra units on existing lots. Pricing a teardown on its current single-house use alone misses that, but paying as if a rezoning were certain means paying for a plan designation, not an approval.
Civic cluster on the land a buyer is act: Civic centre: Maple Ridge Leisure Centre (11925 Haney Place); Memorial Peace Park on 224 Street between Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road, surrounded by City Hall, the ACT Arts Centre and Haney Place Mall, with the Cenotaph, bandstand and Haney Farmers Market; Maple Ridge Public Library (130–22470 Dewdney Trunk Road), the city's only library; and Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre in Haney Place Mall (121–11900 Haney Place, open 7 days, 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.).
Main roads: Lougheed Highway (Highway 7): Main roads: Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) along the south side; Dewdney Trunk Road east–west through downtown and the neighbourhoods to the east; 224 Street and 226 Street, the main north–south streets downtown; and the Haney Bypass, linking Lougheed Highway to Port Haney at the southwest corner.
Transit: Haney Place Exchange is in this: Transit: Haney Place Exchange is in this area, served by routes including the R3, 701, 733, 741, 743, 744, 745, 746, 748, 749 and 791; the R3 Lougheed Highway RapidBus runs from Coquitlam Central Station to Haney Place. Taxes/rebates/financing: PTT 1% / 2% / 3: Taxes, rebates and financing: property transfer tax is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% up to $2 million and 3% above, plus another 2% on the residential part above $3 million. First-time buyers are exempt on the first $500,000 for homes up to $835,000, with a partial exemption up to $860,000; the newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000 and ends at $1,150,000. For example, at $662,500 (the city's condo and townhome median) with no exemption, the tax is $2,000 + $9,250 = $11,250. The first-time buyers' GST rebate (law since March 13, 2026) covers all the GST on a new home up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out at $1.5 million, for agreements from March 20, 2025 to 2031. The GST New Housing Rebate is 36% up to $6,300 (phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000). The Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000, an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000, and CMHC premiums run 0.6%–4.5%. GST applies to new homes, not resales (The Fairways, built in 2007, is a resale), and Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax doesn't apply.

Escarpment / floodplain: The Fraser Rive: Escarpment and floodplain: the Fraser River Escarpment policy area runs from 207 Street on the west to 224 Street on the east, and from 124 Avenue south to the escarpment crest. Properties within 300 m of the crest need a geotechnical report, registered in a covenant, before a building permit, and those within 100 m need a detailed report on earthquake slope failure; septic fields should be avoided, and new homes need sanitary sewer. Hammond fronts the Fraser River: the flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic (including a safety margin), no living space can be below it on affected lots, and suites aren't allowed on floodplain properties.

City zoning/plans: Maple Ridge Zoning By: Zoning (Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019): the standard house zone is RS-1, with a minimum lot of 668.0 m², 18.0 m wide and 27.0 m deep, and up to 40% coverage. Maple Villas' listing shows RM-1.
Current listings (MLS® and (as of Novemb: Current listings show Sherwood Park as two-storey wood-frame strata townhouses built in 1996, with strata fees covering a caretaker, grounds maintenance and management. One listing says "Strata has a strong contingency". Pets are allowed with restrictions; confirm on the Form B.
A current listing (as of November 2, 202: A current listing shows Maple Villas as two-storey wood-frame townhouses built in 1983, zoned RM-1, with strata fees covering grounds maintenance, management and snow removal, and cats and dogs allowed with restrictions; confirm on the Form B.
Form B diligence (both counted complexes: Both complexes are strata, so read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Rental and pet lines in listings aren't the bylaws.
Lougheed Transit Corridor — adopted: the: The Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan was adopted January 27, 2026 (Official Community Plan Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021; the corridor ends at 221 Street). It directs growth around future rapid bus stations along Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road, the street both complexes are on.
West Central's demand signal is in its a: West Central's demand is in its townhomes, not its houses. In September 2026, 3% of detached homes for sale sold, the lowest in the city, while 13% of condos and townhomes sold, from the city's second-largest supply.
Fee-simple lots are the default form: Th: Lots are fee simple: mostly freehold houses on RS-1 lots under Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, with a minimum lot of 668.0 m², 18.0 m wide and 27.0 m deep, and up to 40% coverage.
LOUGHEED TRANSIT CORRIDOR — adopted Jan: The Lougheed Transit Corridor plan (Bylaw 7781-2021) was adopted January 27, 2026, and ends at 221 Street. Don't pay for corridor potential based on the plan alone; check a lot's Town Centre plan designation with the City before valuing it.
Schools: Glenwood Elementary, K-7, 21410: Schools (SD42 Maple Ridge–Pitt Meadows): Glenwood Elementary (K–7), 21410 Glenwood Avenue; Alouette Elementary (K–7), 22155 Isaac Crescent; and Westview Secondary (8–12), 20905 Wicklund Avenue. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
What is actually in the sub-area: Pitt M: What's in the area: Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (1028-18799 Airport Way), with three paved runways and a water runway, run by the Pitt Meadows Airport Society; Harris Landing, at Harris Road and Fraser Way, the start of the Pitt River Greenway (about 10.2 km of dike-top trail along the Fraser and Pitt rivers); and Fraser Way Roundabout Park (19501 Fraser Way). There's no recreation centre, library or public school in the area.
Form B diligence (applies to the strata: The strata townhouses a West Meadows buyer will see, Shoreline and Coho II, are listed under South Meadows. For those, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. There are no strata homes in West Meadows itself.
ALR vs non-ALR, as documented: the City': ALR: the City says 78% of Pitt Meadows is in the Agricultural Land Reserve. The large farms here are zoned A-1 or A-2, in line with the ALR rules; check a specific property's ALR status on the Agricultural Land Commission's maps.
Airport ground is not lot inventory: Pit: The airport isn't land for sale: Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (1028-18799 Airport Way), with three paved runways and a water runway, run by the Pitt Meadows Airport Society, is the area's main neighbour.
Fraser Way / Wildwood Crescent pocket: d: Fraser Way and Wildwood Crescent: detached houses at the east edge, zoned RS Large Lot Residential (minimum lot 0.2 ha) or R-3, R-4 and R-6 Urban Residential (up to 3, 4 or 6 units per lot, with the sixth unit in R-6 only if one unit is adaptable; 1,215 m² minimum for new lots). The RS zone allows a secondary suite or a garden suite (one per lot, 33–90 m²), but not both.
Civic anchors: Harris Landing, at Harris: Landmarks: Harris Landing, at Harris Road and Fraser Way, is the start of the Pitt River Greenway (about 10.2 km along the Fraser and Pitt River dikes), and Fraser Way Roundabout Park is at 19501 Fraser Way. There's no recreation centre, library, shopping centre or grocery store in the area; the Family Recreation Centre (12027 Harris Road) and the city's only library (200-12099 Harris Road) are just east of Harris Road, and the nearest shopping is Meadowtown (19800 Lougheed Highway, Real Canadian Superstore) and Meadowvale (Harris Road, Save-On-Foods). The nearest hospital is Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, Maple Ridge.
The farm parcels: Farm houses on large a: The farms: farm houses on large parcels along Ford Road and Airport Way, zoned A-1 General Agricultural or A-2 Large Lot Agricultural. A-1 allows one farm house per lot (up to 500 m²), plus one more for farms over 8 ha and under 40 ha (two if 40 ha or more), with an 8 ha minimum for new lots; homes must be 15.0 m from watercourses and main ditches. A-2 protects large-lot farming, with a 16 ha minimum for new lots. These are zone rules, not actual lot sizes; check a specific property's area, zone and ALR status on title and the Agricultural Land Commission's maps.
Flood / dikes / ALR / airport: The City: Flooding, dikes, ALR and the airport: the city is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes, plus ditches, pump stations and flood boxes; this part of the city (Kennedy drainage, Area 3) drains to the Alouette, Pitt and Fraser rivers, and A-1 homes must be 15.0 m from watercourses and main ditches. 78% of Pitt Meadows is in the Agricultural Land Reserve. Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (1028-18799 Airport Way), with three paved runways and a water runway, is in this area; the City has a page for safety and noise concerns.
A townhome pocket exists along Fraser Wa: There are townhomes along Fraser Way west of Harris Road, but I don't know the complex's name. Any purchase there is a strata purchase: check the Form B, the depreciation report (for 5 or more units), the contingency reserve and the registered bylaws.
Form B diligence (the frame, if a strata: If a strata townhouse ever sells here, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. There are no strata complexes in Whonnock today.
The stock that does exist here is fee-si: Homes here are fee-simple acreages, with no strata, Form B or strata fees; City zoning (Bylaw No. 7600-2019), ALR rules where they apply, and registered covenants apply instead. Don't expect strata rules on a Whonnock acreage, or strata fees on a fee-simple townhouse.
Market context: Maple Ridge community co: For Maple Ridge as a whole in September 2026: 410 detached homes listed and 40 sold, at a median of $1,131,000, 97% of list price and 29 days on the market; 286 condos and townhomes listed and 33 sold, at a median of $525,000, 94% of list and 49 days. There are no separate figures for land.
ALR rules for Whonnock's agricultural la: On Whonnock's farmland in the ALR: subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, and homes can't be stratified. One main house per parcel, up to 500 m², with a suite only inside it, plus one additional home of up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² on larger ones. For farm tax status, you need farm income of $10,000 on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, or $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha, with applications due by October 31.
Main roads and transit: Lougheed Highway: Roads and transit: Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) and Dewdney Trunk Road run east–west, 272 Street and 280 Street north–south, and 112 Avenue east–west. Route 701 (Coquitlam Central Station / Haney Place / Maple Ridge East / Mission City Station) runs east on Dewdney Trunk Road; most eastbound trips end at Dewdney Trunk Road and 248 Street, and some weekday trips run non-stop from Haney Place to Mission City Station. There's no West Coast Express station here; the nearest are Port Haney and Maple Meadows to the west and Mission City to the east.
